method: Round 1: researcher + source-fidelity verifier + adversarial skeptic per track. Rounds 2-3: live-search audit of every claim, second opinion on contradicted claims. Tags computed by team/merge_audit.py.
tag_rules:
Merge live-audit results (rounds 2 and 3) into the round-1 ledger and write per-track writer payloads.

Usage: python3 merge_audit.py LEDGER.json OUT_DIR AUDIT_RESULT.json [AUDIT_RESULT.json ...]
AUDIT_RESULT files are live-audit.mjs workflow outputs. A later file fills in claims an earlier file left
not_checked or budget_blocked; it never overrides a completed check.

Tagging rules (deterministic):
  confirmed    -> HIGH needs strength=strong, or a live-research track whose claim both round-1 verifiers supported;
                  otherwise MED. weak strength caps at MED.
  corrected    -> MED, corrected wording/citation applied.
  contradicted -> second opinion: contradicted => dropped; supported => CONFLICT; unclear/missing => LOW (disputed).
  not_found    -> live-research track: capped at MED; memory-only track: LOW.
  not_checked / budget_blocked -> live-research track: round-1 tag kept; memory-only track: capped at MED.

claims.claim: Two-photon calcium imaging of the ventral nerve cord in tethered, singing males shows one neural population active during both pulse and sine song, and a larger population, which includes the first, active during pulse song. dPR1 neurons are active only during pulse song; TN1A neurons are active during both songs.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, adult male, tethered singing preparation
claims.source_title: Activity of nested neural circuits drives different courtship songs in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Shiozaki HM, Wang K, Lillvis JL, Xu M, Dickson BJ, Stern DL
notes: live audit: Search results confirm Shiozaki, Wang, Lillvis, Xu, Dickson and Stern, 'Activity of nested neural circuits drives different courtship songs in Drosophila', Nat Neurosci 2024. The results say VNC calcium imaging in behaving flies found different songs produced by 'activating overlapping neural populations', and that 'nested activity patterns displayed by dPR1 and TN1A neurons are a general feature of the song circuit in the VNC.' No result states the exact split (dPR1 pulse-only, TN1A both songs), but the nesting matches the claim.

claims.claim: Optogenetic activation of the descending neuron pIP10 produces both pulse and sine song, while activation of the descending neuron pMP2 produces pulse song but not sine song. Both project heavily into the wing neuropils of the nerve cord.
claims.source_title: Activity of nested neural circuits drives different courtship songs in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Shiozaki HM, Wang K, Lillvis JL, Xu M, Dickson BJ, Stern DL
notes: live audit: Result text says directly: 'Optogenetic activation of pIP10 induces both pulse and sine song, whereas pMP2 activation leads to pulse but not sine song.' That text is from the preprint and paper summary. No result shows the part about heavy projections into the wing neuropils.

claims.claim: Brain recordings show the same nested activation pattern in the two descending pathways needed for singing. The authors also recorded pIP10 calcium signals together with song sound (the signal combines left and right pIP10). Connectome analysis shows these two descending pathways feed structured input to VNC neurons, matching the activation patterns.
claims.source_title: Activity of nested neural circuits drives different courtship songs in Drosophila (PMC full text)
claims.source_authors: Shiozaki HM et al.
notes: live audit: The PMC full text exists (PMC11452343). The results confirm two descending pathways: pIP10 is active whatever the song type, and the pathway that includes pMP2 is active only during pulse song. The details about combined left/right pIP10 signals and the connectome's structured input to VNC neurons are not visible in the results.

claims.claim: The 2022 bioRxiv preprint of this work (titled 'Combinatorial circuit dynamics...') described two descending pathways with different roles: pIP10 is active for both songs, so it acts as a general 'sing' signal, and pMP2 is pulse-selective. The published 2024 Nature Neuroscience paper keeps this idea of distinct descending signals and calls the VNC activity pattern 'nested' instead of 'combinatorial.' The exact 'when vs. what' wording of the preprint is not verified.
claims.source_title: Combinatorial circuit dynamics orchestrate flexible motor patterns in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Shiozaki HM et al. (preprint)
claims.corrected_citation: Shiozaki HM, Wang K, Lillvis JL, Xu M, Dickson BJ, Stern DL. Combinatorial circuit dynamics orchestrate flexible motor patterns in Drosophila. bioRxiv 2022.12.14.520499 (2022); published as Nat Neurosci 2024.
notes: live audit: The 'when vs. what' wording that round 1 left unverified now shows up in the preprint result text: 'song is driven by two descending pathways - one defines when to sing and the other specifies what song to sing.' The caveat can be dropped. v1 of the preprint had a different title: 'Neural coding of distinct motor patterns during Drosophila courtship song'.

claims.claim: Silencing and activation screens identified eight fru- and/or dsx-expressing cell types (pIP10, pMP2, dPR1, dMS9, vMS12, TN1A, dMS2, vPR9), each needed for normal pulse song, sine song, or both. In the MANC connectome (wiring only, one male) they are densely interconnected and connected to wing motor neurons, forming two nested feed-forward pathways with reciprocal and feedback links. The larger pathway underlies pulse song, which the authors argue is the more complex and ancestral song type.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, adult male (MANC connectome for wiring)
claims.source_title: Nested neural circuits generate distinct acoustic signals during Drosophila courtship
claims.source_authors: Lillvis JL, Wang K, Shiozaki HM, Xu M, Stern DL, Dickson BJ
notes: live audit: Lillvis, Wang, Shiozaki, Xu, Stern and Dickson, Curr Biol, Jan 2024, confirmed. Result text: 'The song circuit is organized into two nested feedforward pathways with extensive reciprocal and feedback connections, with the larger network producing pulse song, the more complex and ancestral song form.' It also confirms the authors used cell-type-specific reagents plus the connectome, with activation and inhibition of each cell type. The list of eight named cell types is not visible in the results.

claims.claim: Song-type roles are not cleanly separated. Manipulating the 'pulse' neurons dMS9 and vMS12 also changed sine amplitude or frequency. Manipulating the 'sine' neurons TN1A and dMS2 also changed pulse features. pIP10 and vPR9 affected many features of both song types.
claims.source_title: Nested neural circuits generate distinct acoustic signals during Drosophila courtship (PDF)
claims.source_authors: Lillvis JL et al.
notes: live audit: The source and topic match: activating or inhibiting each cell type and measuring song effects. The cross-mode effects for dMS9, vMS12, TN1A, dMS2, pIP10 and vPR9 are not visible in the results, so they still rest on the single round-1 check. The PDF URL cited in the claim did not appear in any result; the fulltext URL did.

claims.claim: In isolated males, optogenetic activation of dMS9, vMS12, vPR6 or vPR13 produced some sine song, but silencing any one of them did not noticeably reduce sine song. So, for sine song, vPR6 activation can evoke it, but vPR6 has not been shown to be needed for it. Its role in pulse song is a separate question.
claims.source_title: Nested neural circuits generate distinct acoustic signals during Drosophila courtship
claims.source_authors: Lillvis JL et al.
notes: live audit: The source exists and covers activation and silencing of VNC song cell types. Nothing in the results shows the specific finding (dMS9/vMS12/vPR6/vPR13 activation evokes some sine song, but silencing does not reduce it). The claim is LOW confidence and still unconfirmed at the detail level. vPR6 is not among the eight core types in the related T01-05 claim, so check the figure before relying on this.

claims.claim: Five classes of fruitless neurons trigger or make up the song. In the brain, P1 and the descending neuron pIP10 mediate the decision to sing and acting on it. In the thorax, dPR1, vPR6 and vMS11 are proposed parts of a pattern generator that times and shapes song pulses. P1, pIP10 and dPR1 are male-specific.
claims.source_title: Neuronal Control of Drosophila Courtship Song
claims.source_authors: von Philipsborn AC, Liu T, Yu JY, Masser C, Bidaye SS, Dickson BJ
notes: live audit: Source confirmed: von Philipsborn AC, Liu T, Yu JY, Masser C, Bidaye SS, Dickson BJ, Neuron 69(3):509-522, 10 Feb 2011. The search summary states the key finding directly: five classes of fru neurons trigger or make up the song; P1 and pIP10 in the brain mediate the decision to sing; thoracic dPR1, vPR6 and vMS11 are parts of a central pattern generator that times and shapes pulses. The results did not show the detail that P1, pIP10 and dPR1 are male-specific, but nothing contradicts it. The listed ScienceDirect URL (S0896627311000572) also appeared in the results.

claims.claim: Optogenetic stimulation of fruitless-expressing neurons in the thoracic-abdominal ganglia (nerve cord) produces wing movement and sound in both sexes. It produces authentic song only in males, or in females made to express male fruitless. So a song-like motor program exists in females but lies dormant because the commands to start song are missing.
claims.source_title: Sex-Specific Control and Tuning of the Pattern Generator for Courtship Song in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Clyne JD, Miesenbock G
notes: live audit: Source confirmed: Clyne JD, Miesenbock G, Cell 133(2):354-363, 18 Apr 2008 (Yale/Oxford). The results confirm the method: light-activated channels were used to stimulate fru-expressing neurons in the thoracic-abdominal ganglia to compare the sexes. The specific findings (sound in both sexes, authentic song only in males or FruM-expressing females) were not visible in the result text. The closing inference ('dormant because the commands to start song are missing') is the claim's own interpretation and should be worded as one.

claims.claim: The male-specific, doublesex-expressing thoracic interneurons TN1A are needed specifically for sine song. They can drive the wing motor neuron hg1, which is not sex-specific and is also needed for sine song. doublesex acting in TN1A increases TN1A branch density where hg1 dendrites sit, which supports the TN1A-hg1 connection.
claims.source_title: Doublesex Regulates the Connectivity of a Neural Circuit Controlling Drosophila Male Courtship Song
claims.source_authors: Shirangi TR, Wong AM, Truman JW, Stern DL
notes: live audit: Source confirmed: Shirangi TR, Wong AM, Truman JW, Stern DL, Developmental Cell, published 20 Jun 2016 (Janelia). The venue correction to Developmental Cell is right. The results directly state that the male-specific TN1A thoracic interneurons are needed specifically for sine song, that doublesex acts in TN1A to increase arbor density where hg1 motoneuron dendrites sit, and that this promotes TN1A-hg1 connectivity. hg1 is described as sex-non-specific.

claims.claim: Calcium imaging of wing muscles during song shows the direct control muscles i1, hg1-4 and b3 are all strongly active during pulse song. Song and flight use different patterns of muscle activity from a shared set of muscles and motor neurons, and the flight command overrides song.
claims.source_title: Multifunctional Wing Motor Control of Song and Flight
claims.source_authors: O'Sullivan A, Lindsay T, Prudnikova A, Erdi B, Dickinson M, von Philipsborn AC
notes: live audit: Source confirmed: O'Sullivan A, Lindsay T, Prudnikova A, Erdi B, Dickinson M, von Philipsborn AC, Current Biology 28(17):2705-2717.e4, 2018 (online 23 Aug 2018). The results confirm live imaging of muscle ensemble activity during song and flight, a shared small set of wing muscles and motor neurons, and motor neuron silencing experiments. The specific muscle list (i1, hg1-4, b3 strongly active in pulse song) and the claim that flight overrides song were not visible in the result text.

claims.claim: Male D. melanogaster song has at least three modes, not two: fast pulse (Pfast), slow pulse (Pslow) and sine. Pfast is louder and more common when the male is far from the female. Activity of identified song premotor and motor neurons affects which mode is chosen, and the two pulse types affect female behavior differently.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, adult male (sender) and female (receiver)
neurons: song-pathway premotor and motor neurons (identities not given in snippet)
claims.source_title: Discovery of a New Song Mode in Drosophila Reveals Hidden Structure in the Sensory and Neural Drivers of Behavior
claims.source_authors: Clemens J, Coen P, Roemschied FA, Pereira TD, Mazumder D, Aldarondo DE, Pacheco DA, Murthy M
notes: live audit: Source confirmed: Clemens J, Coen P, Roemschied FA, Pereira TD, Mazumder D, Aldarondo DE, Pacheco DA, Murthy M, Current Biology 28(15):2400-2412, 2018. The results directly state at least three song modes (two distinct pulse types plus sine), that visual feedback changes the probability of each mode, and that four separate neuron types in the song pathway affect mode probability differently. The results did not show the loudness and distance details for Pfast or the different female responses to the two pulse types.

claims.claim: Male song patterning is not a fixed action pattern. Males use fast changes in visual and self-motion feedback cues (his own locomotion as well as the female's movement and their distance) to choose song moment by moment. The authors found the same relationship in the other Drosophila species they tested.
claims.source_title: Dynamic sensory cues shape song structure in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Coen P, Clemens J, Weinstein AJ, Pacheco DA, Deng Y, Murthy M
notes: live audit: Coen, Clemens, Weinstein, ..., Murthy, Nature 2014 (507:233) confirmed. Results: males use fast changes in sensory information (visual and self-motion inputs) to actively pattern song, which challenges the fixed-action-pattern view. Results also note that females change walking speed in response to song features. The last sentence, that the same relationship held in other Drosophila species, is NOT visible in any result. Verify it or drop it.

claims.claim: An unsupervised hidden-state model finds three hidden internal states in courting males. Each state maps female feedback cues onto song modes differently, and the model predicts moment-to-moment song choices. Activating a pair of neurons earlier described as song command neurons (likely pIP10) is enough to switch the male between states.
neurons: pIP10 (reported as previously-described song command neurons)
claims.source_title: Unsupervised identification of the internal states that shape natural behavior
claims.source_authors: Calhoun AJ, Pillow JW, Murthy M
notes: live audit: Source confirmed: Calhoun AJ, Pillow JW, Murthy M, Nature Neuroscience 22(12):2040-2049, 2019 (online 25 Nov 2019). An Author Correction exists (s41593-019-0571-4). The results directly state: three latent states, each a different mapping from feedback cues to song modes, moment-to-moment prediction of song choices, and a pair of neurons earlier thought to be song command neurons is enough to switch states. The results did not name pIP10, so the claim's hedge 'likely pIP10' is appropriate.

claims.claim: Males sing simple single-mode trains far from the female and complex pulse-sine alternations near her. VNC song circuits show mutual inhibition and rebound excitability between the nodes that drive the two modes. pC2 neurons drive pulse song directly via pIP10 (simple song from brief input) and also recruit persistent P1a activity and disinhibit the VNC rebound circuit, enabling complex bouts. Unverified here: whether this paper shows P1a being driven by taste cues from tapping.
claims.source_title: Flexible circuit mechanisms for context-dependent song sequencing
claims.source_authors: Roemschied FA, Pacheco DA, Aragon MJ, Ireland EC, Li X, Thieringer K, Pang R, Murthy M
notes: live audit: Results state directly: simple single-mode trains far from the female, complex alternations near her; VNC circuits shaped by mutual inhibition and rebound excitability; brief input to a direct brain-to-VNC excitatory pathway drives simple song, while prolonged input enables complex song through functional disinhibition; P1a mediates disinhibition, not direct excitation, of the VNC rebound circuit. The result text does not name pC2 or pIP10 explicitly. No result mentions taste cues from tapping, so the claim is right to leave that unverified.

claims.claim: pC2l neurons in the central brain respond to both sound and visual cues. In males, activating a subset of them triggers pulse song right away, followed by sine song after activation ends, and pC2l is needed for normal singing. In females, the same type is needed for normal responses to male song.
claims.source_title: Shared Song Detector Neurons in Drosophila Male and Female Brains Drive Sex-Specific Behaviors
claims.source_authors: Deutsch D, Clemens J, Thiberge SY, Guan G, Murthy M
notes: live audit: Source confirmed: Deutsch D, Clemens J, Thiberge SY, Guan G, Murthy M, Current Biology 29(19):3200-3215.e5, Oct 2019. The results confirm that pC2 neurons are tuned to several temporal features of one song mode, that song tuning is similar in both sexes, and that pC2 drives sex-specific behaviors. The finer claims were not visible in the result text: visual responses, pulse song during activation then sine song after offset in males, and pC2l being needed for singing and for female song responses. One PubMed hit (37699336) and one cell.com URL carry 2023 identifiers and are probably a correction notice, so cite the 2019 ScienceDirect or bioRxiv 366765 record.

claims.claim: Courting males produce both airborne song and substrate-borne vibration, mostly in different behavioural contexts. The brain neurons P1a and pC2l can drive both signals through separate premotor pathways with cell-type-specific dynamics. A circuit model with recurrence and mutual inhibition explains why vibration is limited to contexts, such as a close or stationary female, where it is likely to be effective. The exact male counts come from the paper's figures and were not verified here.
claims.source_title: A neural circuit for context-dependent multimodal signaling in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Steinfath E, ... Clemens J
claims.corrected_citation: Steinfath E, Khalili A, Stenger M, Schultze BL, Ravindran Nair S, Alizadeh K, Clemens J. A neural circuit for context-dependent multimodal signaling in Drosophila. Nature Communications 16:9472 (2025; published 27 Oct 2025). Preprint: bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.12.04.625245.
notes: live audit: The paper exists as cited. Result text: males produce air-borne song and substrate-borne vibration 'in distinct, largely non-overlapping contexts'; the same brain neurons that drive song also control vibration through separate premotor pathways with cell-type-specific dynamics; the circuit uses recurrence and mutual inhibition so that vibration is produced only when it can effectively reach the female. The result text does not name P1a or pC2l, so that detail is still unconfirmed. The full author list is now captured. Model code is at github janclemenslab/vibmodel.

claims.claim: Using real-time closed-loop optogenetics, the male's song was made to trigger backward walking in the female (activation of Moonwalker descending neurons), which perturbed her feedback. Males trained this way later changed the contexts in which they sang to new females. This is usage learning of an innate song.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, male sender and optogenetically controlled female receiver
claims.source_title: Recent social experience alters song behavior in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Roemschied FA, Ireland EC, Calhoun AJ, Choi M, Ahmed OM, Murthy M
notes: live audit: Roemschied, Ireland, Calhoun, Choi, Ahmed and Murthy, Current Biology, March 2026, confirmed. Preprint: bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.09.04.674308. A Nature Reviews Neuroscience highlight ('Flies change their tune...') also exists. The results confirm closed-loop optogenetics, adaptive song changes and the term 'usage learning'. They also show the changes are only initially retained and then gradually revert; the claim should say this. The Moonwalker/backward-walking manipulation is not visible in the results.

claims.claim: Optogenetic or thermogenetic activation of P1 neurons in solitary males quickly triggers courtship song that can persist for minutes after stimulation ends (Inagaki et al. 2014; Bath et al. 2014). Hoopfer et al. 2015 show that P1 activation also drives a persistent state that increases inter-male aggression.
claims.source_title: P1 interneurons promote a persistent internal state that enhances inter-male aggression in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Hoopfer ED, Jung Y, Inagaki HK, Rubin GM, Anderson DJ
claims.corrected_citation: Primary: Inagaki HK, Jung Y, Hoopfer ED, Wong AM, Mishra N, Lin JY, Tsien RY, Anderson DJ (2014) 'Optogenetic control of Drosophila using a red-shifted channelrhodopsin reveals experience-dependent influences on courtship.' Nature Methods 11:325-332; Bath DE, Stowers JR, Hormann D, Poehlmann A, Dickson BJ, Straw AD (2014) 'FlyMAD: rapid thermogenetic control of neuronal activity in freely walking Drosophila.' Nature Methods 11:756-762. Secondary: Hoopfer et al. (2015) eLife 4:e11346.
notes: live audit: The Hoopfer et al. 2015 eLife results state: 'Brief optogenetic activation of P1 neurons drives both persistent song production in solitary males and persistent aggression upon introduction of another male, both over minutes (Bath et al., 2014; Hoopfer et al., 2015; Inagaki et al., 2014).' They also say singing persists for minutes after stimulation offset. The round-1 corrected citation (Inagaki 2014 and Bath 2014, both Nature Methods, as primary sources) matches this.

claims.claim: In tethered males courting a fictive female (a dot target in virtual reality), P1 neurons became strongly active at courtship onset, stayed elevated through a courtship bout, and returned to baseline whenever the male paused pursuit.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, adult male, tethered virtual-reality courtship
claims.source_title: An arousal-gated visual circuit controls pursuit during Drosophila courtship (preprint of Nature 2021 'Sexual arousal gates visual processing during Drosophila courtship')
claims.source_authors: Hindmarsh Sten T, Li R, Otopalik A, Ruta V
claims.corrected_citation: Hindmarsh Sten T, Li R, Otopalik A, Ruta V. Sexual arousal gates visual processing during Drosophila courtship. Nature 595:549-553 (2021).
notes: live audit: The published version 'Sexual arousal gates visual processing during Drosophila courtship' appeared in a result on nature.com, which matches the round-1 corrected citation (Nature 2021). The bioRxiv preprint URL and the specific P1 time-course finding were not seen in any result. This check was incidental; no dedicated search was run.

claims.claim: The complete male central nervous system connectome contains about 166,700 fully proofread neurons across brain and nerve cord, annotated for fruitless and doublesex expression, with about 11,700 cell types. Compared with the female brain it has 8,069 matching types, 138 dimorphic types, 289 male-specific and 71 female-specific types. These counts are from the Cell summary; the preprint reported 262 sex-specific plus 114 dimorphic types.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, one adult male (whole CNS, EM)
claims.source_title: Sexual dimorphism in the complete Drosophila male central nervous system connectome
claims.source_authors: Berg S et al. (FlyEM/Janelia, Cambridge, Google)
notes: live audit: Cell 2026 paper confirmed; PubMed 42691995; preprint bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.10.09.680999, whose title word order differs: 'Sexual dimorphism in the complete connectome of the Drosophila male central nervous system'. Result text: 166,700 neurons, fully proofread and annotated including fru/dsx expression; 11,710 neuron types; 8,069 isomorphic, 138 dimorphic, 289 male-specific and 71 female-specific types. Also: sex-specific/dimorphic types make up 4.8% of male and 2.4% of female central-brain neurons. The preprint figures (262 sex-specific plus 114 dimorphic) were not seen in any result. The Janelia and HHMI release reports about 125 million synapses and a September 2026 publication.

claims.claim: In the male CNS versus female brain connectome comparison (wiring only, one animal per sex), sex-specific and dimorphic cell types are concentrated in higher-order central brain regions, while sensory and motor neurons within the CNS are largely similar between sexes. Known exceptions include some sensory afferents. The authors interpret dimorphic neurons as routing shared sensory input into sex-specific behavioural circuits.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, male vs female connectomes
claims.source_title: Sexual dimorphism in the complete Drosophila male central nervous system connectome
claims.source_authors: Berg S et al.
notes: live audit: Result text: 'Sex-specific and dimorphic neurons are concentrated in higher-order brain centers, while the sensory and motor periphery is largely isomorphic', plus a 'high (but not perfect) correspondence between dimorphism status and fru/dsx expression.' The interpretation that dimorphic neurons route shared sensory input into sex-specific circuits is not stated in the result text. The one-animal-per-sex caveat is appropriate.

claims.claim: The Janelia release highlights male pC1 neurons, a diverse dsx+ population (some also fru+) that includes the male-specific P1 subtypes, as promoting courtship song and aggression, based on earlier causal studies. pC1 neurons also exist in females, with different subtypes and roles, and the connectome itself is wiring only.
claims.source_title: Researchers reveal connectome of the male fruit fly central nervous system
claims.source_authors: Janelia Research Campus news
notes: live audit: The Janelia news page exists. Results describe 'male-specific pC1 neurons, a diverse population expressing doublesex and, in some cases, also fruitless, [that] promote courtship song and aggression.' The results also mention a connectome-derived disinhibitory module (vPN1 inhibits male-specific mAL, which inhibits pC1) that may switch behaviour between aggression and courtship, and a vPN1-to-pC1 labeled line for courtship-song hearing. The summary merges several pages, so the text cannot be pinned to the news release rather than the Cell paper. The claim's caveats (female pC1 exists; wiring only) are appropriate.

claims.claim: In the MANC connectome (Cheong et al., eLife 2024), circuits from descending neurons to premotor and motor neurons were systematically mapped, and courtship-linked VNC types including TN1a, dPR1, vPR9 and vMS11 were identified. How older driver-line names (e.g., vPR6) map onto MANC types is not fully settled in the sources seen.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, adult male nerve cord (EM)
claims.source_title: Organization of circuits linking descending input to motor output in the Drosophila Male Adult Nerve Cord connectome
claims.source_authors: Cheong HSJ et al.
claims.venue: eLife (reviewed preprint 2024; version of record reported 2026)
claims.corrected_citation: Cheong HSJ, Eichler K, Sturner T, ..., Card GM. Organization of circuits linking descending input to motor output in the Drosophila Male Adult Nerve Cord connectome. eLife 13:RP96084 (version of record 20 July 2026; reviewed preprint 2024 titled 'Transforming descending input into behavior: The organization of premotor circuits in the Drosophila Male Adult Nerve Cord connectome'; bioRxiv 10.1101/2023.06.07.543976).
notes: live audit: The round-1 corrected_citation uses the old reviewed-preprint title. The version of record (PubMed 42474298, PMC13384506) is titled 'Organization of circuits linking descending input to motor output...' and was published 20 July 2026. Cite the version of record and give 2026 as the year. The topic (DN-to-premotor-to-MN modular organization in MANC) is confirmed. The courtship cell types named in the claim (TN1a, dPR1, vPR9, vMS11) are not visible in the results.

claims.claim: A 2026 preprint aligns connectomes using network structure alone. It uses two complete male VNC connectomes as references to assign cell types to about 13,000 female VNC neurons, flag sex-specific and dimorphic types, and study female counterparts of the male song-production circuit.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, male and female VNC connectomes
neurons: male song circuit VNC types and female counterparts
claims.source_title: Uncovering Sex Differences in the Drosophila Ventral Nerve Cord Through Connectome Alignment
claims.source_authors: (authors not captured in search results)
notes: live audit: The preprint exists (June 2026; also PubMed 42367857 and PMC13307954). Result text: the method aligns connectomes by network topology alone and uses two complete male VNC connectomes as references to assign cell types to about 13,000 neurons intrinsic to the female VNC. It automatically identifies sex-specific and dimorphic types, focusing on male song-production circuits and female oviposition circuits. Authors still not captured. Better wording would say the study compares song circuits across sexes and also covers oviposition circuits, rather than 'female counterparts' only.

claims.claim: The homologous male-specific descending neuron pIP10 (one per hemisphere) was genetically targeted in D. melanogaster and D. yakuba. Its activation gave different song types in the two species: sine in D. melanogaster at low activation, 'clack' song in D. yakuba, and more pulse in D. yakuba at higher activation. The evolutionary change was placed downstream of pIP10's own physiology.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster and D. yakuba, adult males
claims.source_title: Neural Evolution of Context-Dependent Fly Song
claims.source_authors: Ding Y, Lillvis JL, Cande J, Berman GJ, Arthur BJ, Long X, Xu M, Dickson BJ, Stern DL
notes: live audit: Ding, Lillvis, Cande, Berman, Arthur, Long, Xu, Dickson and Stern, Curr Biol, 1 April 2019 (PubMed 30880014), confirmed. Results confirm pIP10 was genetically targeted in both species, the D. yakuba 'clack' song, and that the evolutionary change lies downstream of the descending neurons' intrinsic physiology. The visible headline finding is from silencing: inhibiting pIP10 mainly reduced pulse song in D. melanogaster and clack song in D. yakuba, song types produced in a conserved context (fast chasing at a distance). The claim omits this. The activation-level details (sine at low activation in melanogaster; more pulse at high activation in yakuba) are not visible.

claims.claim: D. yakuba, which lost sine song, lacks a TN1A-equivalent cell type. Its TN1 neurons can still drive the singing wing posture but not sine song. A divergent doublesex function in D. yakuba reduces TN1 number by promoting cell death.
claims.species: Drosophila yakuba vs D. melanogaster, adult males
claims.source_title: Changes in the cellular makeup of motor patterning circuits drive courtship song evolution in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Ye D, Walsh JT, Junker IP, Ding Y
claims.corrected_citation: Ye D, Walsh JT, Junker IP, Ding Y. Changes in the cellular makeup of motor patterning circuits drive courtship song evolution in Drosophila. Current Biology 34(11):2319-2329 (2024).
notes: live audit: Result text says directly: D. yakuba 'specifically lacks a cell type corresponding to TN1A neurons'; loss of sine song goes with fewer TN1 neurons and fewer sine-circuit neurites; a divergent doublesex function in D. yakuba reduces TN1 number by promoting apoptosis. That TN1 in yakuba can still drive the singing wing posture is not visible in the results.

claims.claim: Activating doublesex-expressing neurons in the female brain, with the pC1 cluster identified as critical, makes females court like males: mainly orienting and following, with occasional tapping and one-wing extension. Audio recordings show male-like song features, including sine and pulse episodes. The female brain therefore contains latent circuitry for male-like courtship and song.
claims.source_title: Brain wiring explains sex differences in Drosophila behaviour (JEB summary of Rezaval et al. 2016)
claims.source_authors: Rezaval C et al. (2016), summarized in Journal of Experimental Biology
claims.venue: Journal of Experimental Biology (secondary summary); primary paper Current Biology 2016
claims.corrected_citation: Rezaval C, Pattnaik S, Pavlou HJ, Nojima T, Bruggemeier B, D'Souza LAD, Dweck HKM, Goodwin SF (2016). Activation of Latent Courtship Circuitry in the Brain of Drosophila Females Induces Male-like Behaviors. Current Biology 26(18):2508-2515. doi:10.1016/j.cub.2016.07.021
notes: live audit: The claim cites a secondary JEB summary; the primary paper was located (PubMed 27568592, PMC5049544, Cell URL S0960-9822(16)30772-2), so cite that instead. The findings are confirmed: song-like acoustic output with sine and pulse episodes, and dsx+ pC1 as the latent circuit. The corrected wording adds that following and orienting dominate, while tapping and wing extension are occasional.

claims.claim: D. melanogaster females produce a copulation song by wing vibration during mating. It differs from male courtship song, requires DoublesexF-expressing neurons, and is modulated by seminal fluid from the male. A downstream effect on remating is not verified here.
claims.source_title: Female copulation song is modulated by seminal fluid
claims.source_authors: Kerwin P, Yuan J, von Philipsborn AC
claims.corrected_citation: Kerwin P, Yuan J, von Philipsborn AC. Female copulation song is modulated by seminal fluid. Nature Communications 11:1430 (2020).
notes: live audit: Every part of the claim is stated in the results. The remating effect that the claim leaves unverified is also in the results: 'Playback of female copulation song to a mating couple increases the time the female takes to remate with subsequent males.' Hearing the song also increases a male's reproductive success under competition.

claims.claim: Hearing regulates male-male aggression, and courtship song and aggression song affect aggression differently. Males therefore have an acoustic threat or agonistic signal, but the neurons that produce aggression song were not identified in this work.
claims.source_title: Hearing regulates Drosophila aggression
claims.source_authors: Versteven M, Vanden Broeck L, Geurten B, Zwarts L, Decraecker L, Beelen M, Gopfert MC, Heinrich R, Callaerts P
notes: live audit: Source confirmed: Versteven M, Vanden Broeck L, Geurten B, et al., incl. Gopfert MC, Heinrich R, Callaerts P. PNAS 114(8):1958-1963, 21 Feb 2017 (online 23 Jan 2017), PubMed 28115690. The results directly state that hearing regulates male aggression and that courtship and aggression songs affect aggression differently. A PNAS commentary on it also exists ('Sound and fury', PubMed 28242705).

new_leads_unverified.claim: Male CNS connectome analysis identifies a disinhibitory module in which vPN1 inhibits a male-specific mAL, which in turn inhibits pC1. The authors propose it switches male behaviour between aggression and courtship. They also identify a male-specific vPN1-to-pC1 labeled line for processing courtship song. This is a wiring-based hypothesis, not a causal test.
new_leads_unverified.source_title: Sexual dimorphism in the complete Drosophila male central nervous system connectome
new_leads_unverified.authors: Berg S et al. (FlyEM Janelia, Cambridge Connectomics, Google Research)
new_leads_unverified.why_it_matters: Names a candidate circuit for how the male brain turns heard song into courtship versus aggression. That matters for a two-way communication program, since playback could hit either behaviour, and the track's claims do not cover this module.

new_leads_unverified.claim: A 2025 review covers the neural evolution of complex motor behaviour using Drosophila courtship song across species.
new_leads_unverified.source_title: Neural evolution of complex motor behaviors: insights from Drosophila courtship song
new_leads_unverified.venue: Current Opinion in Neurobiology (inferred from ScienceDirect PII S0959-4388)
new_leads_unverified.why_it_matters: A recent synthesis that ties together the pIP10, TN1A and D. yakuba evolution findings (T01-26 and T01-27); useful as a single citation for the track.

new_leads_unverified.claim: A 2026 Current Biology paper on how distinct wing behaviors are sequenced during Drosophila courtship. It may update the song-production circuit picture (song versus other wing displays) beyond the 2011-2019 sources this track relies on.
new_leads_unverified.source_title: Sequencing of distinct wing behaviors during Drosophila courtship
new_leads_unverified.why_it_matters: A recent primary study on song and wing motor sequencing. The track has no 2025-2026 production-side claims. Authors and findings need checking.

new_leads_unverified.claim: A recent PubMed record (PMID in the 41.7M range, so probably 2026) reports that recent social experience changes Drosophila song behavior.
new_leads_unverified.source_title: Recent social experience alters song behavior in Drosophila
new_leads_unverified.why_it_matters: Song output that depends on experience matters for any two-way playback or communication design, because a sender's signal may shift with social history. Year, venue and authors are unconfirmed.

new_leads_unverified.claim: A 2025 review in a ScienceDirect journal, probably Current Opinion in Neurobiology given the S0959-4388 ISSN, on the neural evolution of complex motor behaviors using Drosophila courtship song.
new_leads_unverified.source_title: Neural evolution of complex motor behaviors: insights from Drosophila courtship song
new_leads_unverified.why_it_matters: An up-to-date synthesis of the song motor circuit (TN1A, hg1, pattern generators) across species. Useful to check that the track's claims are current.

claims.claim: Volumetric pan-neuronal calcium imaging registered across the whole central brain found auditory activity in most central brain regions, including in neurons responsive to other modalities; responses were temporally diverse but the majority were tuned to courtship-song features.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, head-fixed adults, both sexes compared (pan-neuronal GCaMP)
claims.source_title: Auditory activity is diverse and widespread throughout the central brain of Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Pacheco DA, Thiberge SY, Pnevmatikakis E, Murthy M
notes: live audit: Search results give Pacheco DA, Thiberge SY, Pnevmatikakis E, Murthy M, Nature Neuroscience 24(1):93-104 (2021), with a bioRxiv preprint from July 2019 (10.1101/709519). The summary says it outright: volumetric imaging with registration across the whole brain found auditory activity in most central brain regions, including in neurons responsive to other modalities. Responses were temporally diverse, but most activity was tuned to courtship song features. The citation matches.

claims.claim: In the same whole-brain dataset, auditory responses were stereotyped across trials and animals in early mechanosensory regions and became more variable at higher stages of the putative pathway; this variability was largely independent of spontaneous movements.
claims.source_title: Auditory activity is diverse and widespread throughout the central brain of Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Pacheco DA, Thiberge SY, Pnevmatikakis E, Murthy M
notes: live audit: Same source and citation as T02-01, both verified. The results mention the comparisons across trials, individuals and sexes. They do not show the specific finding: stereotyped responses in early mechanosensory regions, more variability at higher stages, and variability mostly independent of movement. This matches what I recall of the abstract, but it was not visible here.

claims.claim: Johnston's organ neurons form five subgroups (JO-A to JO-E). Calcium imaging showed JO-A and JO-B are activated by antennal vibration (sound), while JO-C and JO-E respond most strongly to static antennal deflection. Silencing the A/B neurons impaired hearing (song responses) and silencing the C/E neurons impaired gravitaxis. Only the sound-sensitive neurons express the candidate mechanotransducer channel NompC, and the two subsets project to separate central pathways. (A proposed ~100 Hz frequency split between JO-B and JO-A still needs a primary source.)
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster (calcium imaging of JON subgroups)
claims.source_title: The neural basis of Drosophila gravity-sensing and hearing
claims.source_authors: Kamikouchi A, Inagaki HK, Effertz T, Hendrich O, Fiala A, Goepfert MC, Ito K
claims.corrected_citation: Kamikouchi A, Inagaki HK, Effertz T, Hendrich O, Fiala A, Goepfert MC, Ito K. The neural basis of Drosophila gravity-sensing and hearing. Nature 458(7235):165-171 (2009). doi:10.1038/nature07810. PMID 19279630.
notes: live audit: This is not an error. The original claim was accurate but hedged, and one hedge is now resolved: the abstract (shown in the results) states that 'only the latter [sound-sensitive neurons] express the candidate mechanotransducer channel NompC.' The results confirm the paper, authors and venue (Nature 458:165-171). The subgroup and silencing details were not visible in the result text but match the paper as I remember it, so strength is moderate. The ~100 Hz cut-off was not checked.

claims.claim: Drosophila auditory receptor neurons adapt to stimulus mean and intensity, change their frequency tuning with sound intensity, and apply a quadratic nonlinearity, which together give an efficient representation of courtship song.
claims.source_title: Quadratic and adaptive computations yield an efficient representation of song in Drosophila auditory receptor neurons
claims.source_authors: Clemens J, Murthy M
notes: live audit: Search result text states that the receptor neurons 'adapt to the mean and the intensity of the stimulus, change their frequency tuning with sound intensity, and employ a quadratic nonlinearity'. Authors are Jan Clemens and Mala Murthy (2021), bioRxiv. Code and data are at github.com/janclemenslab/quadratic-adaptive. No journal version appeared in the results, so cite it as a preprint.

claims.claim: Two cell types postsynaptic to antennal vibration receptors (A2 and B1) encode vibration differently. A2 cells receive excitation for both directions of antennal movement (twice per cycle) and their membrane low-pass filters it, so A2 tracks the vibration envelope. B1 cells are phase-sensitive (excited by forward or backward movement only) and band-pass filter oscillatory synaptic input at the stimulus frequency. Different B1 cells prefer different frequencies because of differences in voltage-gated Na+/K+ conductances.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster (in vivo whole-cell patch clamp)
claims.source_title: Active Mechanisms of Vibration Encoding and Frequency Filtering in Central Mechanosensory Neurons
claims.source_authors: Azevedo AW, Wilson RI
claims.corrected_citation: Azevedo AW, Wilson RI. Active Mechanisms of Vibration Encoding and Frequency Filtering in Central Mechanosensory Neurons. Neuron 96(2):446-460 (2017). doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2017.09.004.
notes: live audit: The results state the A2 and B1 findings directly. A2 is excited by both directions of movement (twice per cycle) and low-pass filters that input, so it tracks the envelope. B1 is sensitive to phase (excited by forward or backward movement only), receives oscillatory synaptic currents and band-pass filters them. The final sentence, that different B1 cells prefer different frequencies because of differences in Na+/K+ conductances, was not in the result text but agrees with the abstract as I recall it. The citation only needed the issue and pages added.

claims.claim: Of seven auditory projection neuron types (aPNs) and five local interneuron types (aLNs) of the ascending mechanosensory pathway, only aPN1 (= AMMC-B1) and the GABAergic interneuron aLN(al) were necessary for behavioral song responses, in both males and females.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, males and females (neuronal inactivation/hyperactivation during behavior)
claims.source_title: Neural pathways for the detection and discrimination of conspecific song in D. melanogaster
claims.source_authors: Vaughan AG, Zhou C, Manoli DS, Baker BS
claims.corrected_citation: Vaughan AG, Zhou C, Manoli DS, Baker BS. Neural pathways for the detection and discrimination of conspecific song in D. melanogaster. Current Biology 24(10):1039-1049 (2014).
notes: live audit: The results state it directly: of 7 aPNs and 5 aLNs, only aPN1 and the GABAergic aLN(al) are needed for song responses, in both males and females. The results do not spell out aPN1 = AMMC-B1, but that identification is standard in the field. The claim adds the volume, issue and pages.

claims.claim: AMMC-B1 neurons show inter-pulse-interval (IPI) selectivity that differs from upstream JONs. Two GABAergic AMMC local interneurons receive auditory input and provide feedforward inhibition onto B1 neurons, and are proposed to shape B1 interval selectivity and the female response to song.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, females (calcium imaging/electrophysiology plus behavior)
claims.source_title: GABAergic Local Interneurons Shape Female Fruit Fly Response to Mating Songs
claims.source_authors: Yamada D, Ishimoto H, Li X, Kohashi T, Ishikawa Y, Kamikouchi A
notes: live audit: The citation is confirmed: Yamada D, Ishimoto H, Li X, Kohashi T, Ishikawa Y, Kamikouchi A, J Neurosci 38(18):4329-4347 (2018), doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.3644-17.2018. The results name the two GABAergic interneurons as AMMC-LN and AMMC-B2 and say they shape the AMMC-B1 response pattern by inhibiting activity to short-IPI song. The specific points that B1 selectivity differs from JONs and that the inhibition is feedforward were not visible. Suggest naming AMMC-LN and AMMC-B2 in the claim.

claims.claim: Calcium imaging of newly identified intermediate-layer auditory cell types (WED/VLP), together with known types such as B1 and pC2, showed a continuum of preferences between sine and pulse song modes rather than two separate channels. The '24' count comes from the researcher's source and was not independently confirmed.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster (calcium imaging of identified cell types)
claims.source_title: Neural network organization for courtship-song feature detection in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Baker CA, McKellar C, Pang R, Nern A, Dorkenwald S, Pacheco DA, et al., Murthy M
notes: live audit: Results confirm Baker CA, McKellar C, Pang R, Nern A, Dorkenwald S, Pacheco DA et al., Curr Biol 32(15):3317-3333.e7, 8 Aug 2022. They explicitly state that the authors 'identified 24 new cell types of the intermediate layers of the auditory pathway' and found 'a continuum of preferences for courtship song modes'. The caveat about the '24' count can therefore be dropped. PubMed 35793679.

claims.claim: Mapping synapses among these auditory cell types in FlyWire (adult female FAFB EM) showed that neurons with different song-mode preferences and response timescales are highly interconnected in a network without hierarchical structure. The authors call this the first circuit-level map of the fly auditory pathway and relate it to the imaged tuning. Synapse sign comes from predicted neurotransmitter identity (Eckstein/Funke classifier), not measured physiology.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, adult female (FlyWire/FAFB) with imaging cross-check
claims.source_title: Neural network organization for courtship-song feature detection in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Baker CA, McKellar C, Pang R, Nern A, Dorkenwald S, Pacheco DA, et al., Murthy M
notes: live audit: Results state that the authors mapped all synaptic connections among these types in FlyWire, 'representing the first circuit-level map of the auditory pathway'. Neurons with different song-mode preferences and timescales are 'highly interconnected in a network lacking hierarchical structure', and cell-type responses are predictable from their inputs. The authors 'determined the sign of most synapses'. The results did not show that the signs came from a neurotransmitter classifier, but the claim's caveat on that point is reasonable.

claims.claim: Zhou et al. 2015 used calcium imaging to show that in males, third-order vPN1 neurons prefer pulse song with long IPIs, and fourth-order pC1 responses across IPIs match the IPI tuning of song-induced male chaining. They proposed aPN1 -> vPN1 -> pC1 as the pathway. The 2026 male CNS connectome refines this: vPN1 is GABAergic, so its apparent excitation of pC1 is best explained by disinhibition (vPN1 inhibits the male-specific mAL, which inhibits pC1), not a direct excitatory link.
claims.source_title: Central neural circuitry mediating courtship song perception in male Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Zhou C, Franconville R, Vaughan AG, Robinett CC, Jayaraman V, Baker BS
notes: live audit: The Zhou 2015 source appeared in the results (PMC4575990) but its IPI tuning data were not visible. The male CNS connectome result (Cell 2026, S0092-8674(26)00942-6) summary states that 'vPN1 is GABAergic, so connectomic analysis identifies a disinhibitory circuit where vPN1 inhibits a male-specific mAL, which in turn inhibits pC1.' The 'aPN1 -> vPN1 -> pC1' wording should be qualified accordingly.

claims.claim: Genetic inactivation of vPN1 or pC1 disrupts song-induced male chaining (male-male courtship in response to song playback).
claims.source_title: Central neural circuitry mediating courtship song perception in male Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Zhou C, Franconville R, Vaughan AG, Robinett CC, Jayaraman V, Baker BS
notes: live audit: The source exists (PMC4575990 appeared in the results), but the inactivation and chaining result was not visible. The only indirect support is the 2026 connectome summary saying male-specific vPN1 respond to song and appear to drive pC1 (via disinhibition).

claims.claim: Dsx+ pC2 neurons are tuned for multiple temporal features of pulse song, and song feature tuning is similar in male and female brains. The authors conclude that sex-shared song detectors drive divergent behaviors.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, males and females (calcium imaging)
claims.source_title: Shared Song Detector Neurons in Drosophila Male and Female Brains Drive Sex-Specific Behaviors
claims.source_authors: Deutsch D, Clemens J, Thiberge SY, Guan G, Murthy M
notes: live audit: The ScienceDirect page for Deutsch et al. 2019 Curr Biol appeared in the results. A related result summary (bioRxiv version of the same paper) states that pC2 neurons 'serve as shared pulse song detectors in both sexes, with the tuning of pC2 neurons matched to behavioral tuning for pulse song across a wide range of temporal scales', which is consistent with the claim.

claims.claim: pC2l neurons in both sexes respond selectively to features of pulse song. Silencing pC2l in females reduces female slowing to pulse song. In males, optogenetic activation of a subset of pC2l acutely elicits pulse song, followed by transient sine song after the light goes off. Males with a subset of pC2l silenced still sang pulse song with normal IPIs, pulse shapes and carrier frequencies, but sang about twice as much as controls, mainly more sine song.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, males and females (optogenetic/genetic silencing and activation)
claims.source_title: Shared Song Detector Neurons in Drosophila Male and Female Brains Drive Sex-Specific Behaviors
claims.source_authors: Deutsch D, Clemens J, Thiberge SY, Guan G, Murthy M
claims.corrected_citation: Deutsch D, Clemens J, Thiberge SY, Guan G, Murthy M. Shared Song Detector Neurons in Drosophila Male and Female Brains Drive Sex-Specific Behaviors. Current Biology 29(19):3200-3215.e5 (2019). A correction notice was later indexed (PII S0960-9822(23)01049-7).
notes: live audit: This is not an error. The original claim was accurate but hedged, and the results resolve the hedge on male silencing. They directly state the female silencing result, the male activation result (pulse song during light, sine song after), and the male silencing result (about 2x more singing, driven by sine song, with pulse parameters normal). No effect on mating success was visible, so the corrected claim leaves it out. A 2023 correction notice for this article shows up in the University of Haifa research-catalogue (CRIS) listing.

claims.claim: Female vaginal plate opening (VPO, the acceptance act) is controlled by a pair of female-specific descending neurons (vpoDNs). vpoDNs receive excitatory input from auditory vpoEN neurons, which are tuned to features of D. melanogaster song, and from pC1 neurons, which encode mating status. The synaptic connections were confirmed in EM connectome data.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, females (imaging, optogenetics, EM connectivity)
claims.source_title: Neural circuit mechanisms of sexual receptivity in Drosophila females
claims.source_authors: Wang F, Wang K, et al., Dickson BJ
claims.corrected_citation: Wang K, Wang F, Forknall N, Yang T, Patrick C, Parekh R, Dickson BJ. Neural circuit mechanisms of sexual receptivity in Drosophila females. Nature 589:577-581 (2021).
notes: live audit: Result text directly states that VPO is controlled by a pair of female-specific vpoDNs. These receive excitatory input from auditory vpoENs tuned to D. melanogaster song and from pC1 neurons encoding mating status. Nature 589:577-581 (2021) is confirmed, and the preprint is bioRxiv 2020.08.07.241919. Author order was not visible in the results. Keep round 1's corrected_citation (Wang K first), which differs from the source_authors field (Wang F first).

claims.claim: After mating, vpoDN song responses are attenuated but vpoEN responses are not, and pC1 neurons mediate this change. For vaginal plate opening, the key mating-status gate therefore sits where vpoDN integrates song and state. That does not exclude state-dependent modulation elsewhere in the auditory pathway.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, virgin vs mated females (calcium imaging)
claims.source_title: Neural circuit mechanisms of sexual receptivity in Drosophila females
claims.source_authors: Wang F, Wang K, et al., Dickson BJ
notes: live audit: Result text: 'The song responses of vpoDNs, but not vpoENs, are attenuated upon mating, accounting for the reduced receptivity of mated females', with pC1 encoding mating status. The claim's narrowed wording (gate at vpoDN, without excluding modulation elsewhere) fits this.

claims.claim: Activating pC1 or pCd neurons in females promotes receptivity and silencing them makes females unreceptive. Female pC1 neurons respond both to courtship song and to the male pheromone cVA, consistent with multisensory integration of courtship cues.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, females (thermogenetic/optogenetic manipulation plus calcium imaging)
claims.source_title: Central brain neurons expressing doublesex regulate female receptivity in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Zhou C, Pan Y, Robinett CC, Meissner GW, Baker BS
notes: live audit: The citation is confirmed: Zhou C, Pan Y, Robinett CC, Meissner GW, Baker BS, Neuron 83(1):149-163 (2014). The results state that activating pCd or pC1 promotes receptivity and silencing them makes females unreceptive. Calcium imaging showed that both pCd and pC1 respond to cVA, and pC1 also responds to courtship song. The claim is accurate. It could add that pCd also responds to cVA.

claims.claim: A subset of female Dsx+ pC1 neurons (pC1d/e) can drive minutes-long changes in female behavior in the presence of males. EM reconstruction of all their inputs and outputs revealed strong recurrent connectivity between pC1d/e and Fruitless+ aIPg neurons.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, females (optogenetics plus FAFB EM reconstruction)
claims.source_title: The neural basis for a persistent internal state in Drosophila females
claims.source_authors: Deutsch D, Pacheco D, Encarnacion-Rivera L, et al., Murthy M
notes: live audit: The citation is confirmed: Deutsch D, Pacheco DA, Encarnacion-Rivera L, et al., Murthy M, eLife 9:e59502 (2020), also at PMC7787663. The results directly state that Dsx+ pC1d/e neurons can drive minutes-long changes in female behavior in the presence of males. The EM finding of strong recurrent connectivity between pC1d/e and Fru+ aIPg was not visible in the results, so strength is moderate.

claims.claim: DNp13 descending neurons are command-type neurons for ovipositor extrusion (OE). They respond to male song through direct synaptic input from pC2l auditory neurons. Mating status does not change DNp13 song responses; it changes how effectively they engage OE motor circuits, via ppk+ uterine sensory neurons activated by ovulation.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, females (calcium imaging, optogenetics, EM connectivity)
claims.source_title: Circuit and Behavioral Mechanisms of Sexual Rejection by Drosophila Females
claims.source_authors: Wang F, Wang K, et al., Dickson BJ
notes: live audit: Result text directly states that DNp13 are command-type neurons for OE and respond to song via direct synaptic input from pC2l (about 20 dsx+ cholinergic cells per hemisphere). It also states that mating status does not modulate DNp13 song responses but changes how effectively they engage OE motor circuits, with the mating signal carried by ppk+ uterine sensory neurons activated by ovulation. Curr Biol, August 2020. PubMed 32795445.

claims.claim: Male song is more likely to evoke vaginal plate opening in virgin females and ovipositor extrusion in recently mated females (Wang et al. 2020). The role of OE is disputed: Wang et al. treat it as a rejection behavior in mated females, while the companion paper by Mezzera et al. 2020 reports that OE promotes copulation attempts and signals acceptance in virgins.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, virgin vs mated females
claims.source_title: Circuit and Behavioral Mechanisms of Sexual Rejection by Drosophila Females
claims.source_authors: Wang F, Wang K, et al., Dickson BJ
notes: live audit: The Wang et al. 2020 portion is directly confirmed. Virgins are more likely to open their vaginal plates in response to song and mated females more likely to extrude the ovipositor, which Wang et al. frame as rejection. They also report that OE is an effective deterrent only when performed by previously mated females. The contrasting Mezzera et al. 2020 interpretation was not searched in this session.

claims.claim: Ovipositor extrusion is shown only by sexually mature females, only during courtship, and in response to male song. OE promotes male copulation attempts in both virgin and mated females and signals acceptance in virgins.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, females and responding males
claims.source_title: Ovipositor Extrusion Promotes the Transition from Courtship to Copulation and Signals Female Acceptance in Drosophila melanogaster
claims.source_authors: Mezzera C, Brotas M, Gaspar M, Pavlou HJ, Goodwin SF, Vasconcelos ML
claims.corrected_citation: Mezzera C, Brotas M, Gaspar M, Pavlou HJ, Goodwin SF, Vasconcelos ML. Ovipositor Extrusion Promotes the Transition from Courtship to Copulation and Signals Female Acceptance in Drosophila melanogaster. Current Biology 30(19):3736-3748.e5 (2020).
notes: live audit: The results state both parts directly. OE is shown only by sexually mature females, only during courtship and in response to male song. OE promotes male copulation attempts in virgin and mated females and signals acceptance in virgins. The citation only needed the volume and pages added.

claims.claim: A 2025 iScience study (Kamikouchi-lab/Nagoya) reports that female JONs express several dopamine receptor types. Connectome data suggest some JONs contact dopaminergic neurons directly (wiring evidence). Dop1R2 knockdown in JONs reduced JON sound responses in unmated but not mated females (calcium imaging). Overexpressing Dop1R2 in JONs enhanced unmated females' song-response behavior in the lab's playback assay.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, unmated vs mated females aged 5-7 days (calcium imaging, RNAi, behavior)
claims.source_title: Mating status-dependent dopaminergic modulation of auditory sensory neurons in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Yamakoshi H, Horigome M, Yamamoto S, et al. (Nagoya University)
notes: live audit: Results confirm the iScience paper (published online 29 July 2025; PubMed 40831745; preprint bioRxiv 2025.05.22.655009). Stated findings: JONs abundantly express three dopamine receptor types, and some have direct synapses with dopaminergic neurons. Dop1R2 knockdown reduces JON sound responses in unmated but not mated females. Dop1R2 expression in JONs enhances unmated females' song-response behavior, measured as copulation receptivity when exposed to song. An erratum exists (PubMed 41660267) and should be checked. Author names and the article number 113232 were not visible in the results.

claims.claim: During natural courtship, females are sensitive to long-timescale song structure (tens of seconds) and integrate song information. Simple computations applied to single-neuron responses can predict female locomotor behavior.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, freely courting pairs plus neural recordings
claims.source_title: Connecting Neural Codes with Behavior in the Auditory System of Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Clemens J, Girardin CC, Coen P, Guan XJ, Dickson BJ, Murthy M
claims.corrected_citation: Clemens J, Girardin CC, Coen P, Guan XJ, Dickson BJ, Murthy M. Connecting Neural Codes with Behavior in the Auditory System of Drosophila. Neuron 87(6):1332-1343 (2015). doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2015.08.014.
notes: live audit: The citation is confirmed. The results describe combining natural courtship behavior with recordings from neurons in the female auditory pathway to build a model that correctly predicted the song length females respond to. That supports the claim that computations on neural responses predict female behavior. The 'tens of seconds' timescale was not visible in the result text, so strength is moderate.

claims.claim: Comparing computational models of female song processing against neural activity and unrestrained courtship behavior, the best model used neurons that adapt to and accumulate their inputs, with heterogeneous nonlinear adaptation and slow integration. This let fine-scale song information persist in the population code for long periods.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, females (model fit to recorded neural data and courtship behavior)
claims.source_title: Inferring neural population codes for Drosophila acoustic communication
claims.source_authors: Pang R, Baker CA, Murthy M, Pillow J
notes: live audit: Pang R, Baker CA, Murthy M, Pillow J. PNAS 2025 (also PMC12130820). A linear-nonlinear feature-detection model and a nonlinear accumulation model both explained the neural data, but the accumulation model better predicted female locomotion during courtship. It relied on heterogeneous nonlinear adaptation and slow integration, letting fine-scale song information be retained in the population code for long periods. 'Best model' should be read as best at predicting behavior.

claims.claim: A 2024 iScience study from the Kamikouchi lab with Janelia co-authors (likely Imoto K, ..., Aso Y, Funke J, ..., Kamikouchi A; confirm) reports the following. Song preference learning (reduced response to heterospecific song after hearing conspecific song) requires GABA made in pCd-2 neurons, a small Dsx+ population of about four cells per hemibrain. Female connectome data show direct, often reciprocal, pCd-2-pC1 connections. The sex used for the behavioral experiments, and the dopamine requirement, need confirming from the paper.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, females (RNAi plus connectome analysis)
claims.source_title: Neural-circuit basis of song preference learning in fruit flies
claims.source_authors: Kamikouchi lab (Nagoya) with Janelia co-authors; full author list not confirmed in results
notes: live audit: Results confirm the four dsx+ GABAergic pCd-2 neurons per hemibrain, the requirement for GABAergic input to pC1, direct and often mutual pCd-2-pC1 connections, and a dopamine requirement via Dop1R2 on pCd-2, so that open question is resolved. Published in iScience in June 2024 (preprint bioRxiv 2023.10.24.563693; PMC11260866; Janelia publication page exists). The full author list, including Imoto K, was still not visible in the results.

claims.claim: D. melanogaster and D. simulans females each increase receptivity to songs with conspecific temporal patterns. JONs and AMMC-B1 neurons share morphology and neurotransmitters across the two species, and the early auditory circuit is largely conserved. AMMC-B1 temporal-pattern preferences are relatively similar across species, with slight but significant band-pass differences too small to explain the behavioral difference in song preference. The divergence in preference therefore likely lies downstream of B1.
claims.species: D. melanogaster vs D. simulans females (behavior plus neuroanatomy)
claims.source_title: Evolutionary conservation and diversification of auditory neural circuits that process courtship songs in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Kamikouchi lab (Nagoya); first author not confirmed in results
claims.corrected_citation: Ohashi T, et al. (Kamikouchi lab). Evolutionary conservation and diversification of auditory neural circuits that process courtship songs in Drosophila. Scientific Reports (2023). PMID 36611081; PMC9825394.
notes: live audit: First author is Ohashi (per the search summary). The claim's statement that 'the circuits that set IPI preference have diversified' overstates the paper. The paper reports an overall conserved, slightly divergent early circuit, and B1 differences that cannot account for the behavioral difference. The specific IPI and carrier-frequency numbers (55 ms/320 Hz vs 35 ms/170 Hz) were not visible in the results.

claims.claim: The complete male CNS connectome (Cell 2026; preprint 2025, reportedly Berg, Beckett, Costa, Schlegel et al. with Janelia FlyEM, Cambridge/MRC LMB and Google) reports that sex-specific and dimorphic neuron types concentrate in higher brain centres, while the sensory and motor periphery is largely isomorphic. Cell-type counts should be taken from the final published version only.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, adult male CNS compared with female connectomes
claims.source_title: Sexual dimorphism in the complete Drosophila male central nervous system connectome
claims.source_authors: Janelia FlyEM, MRC LMB, University of Cambridge and Google Research consortium
claims.corrected_citation: Sexual dimorphism in the complete Drosophila male central nervous system connectome. Cell 189(18):5504-5526.e15 (2026), published 3 Sep 2026. doi:10.1016/j.cell.2026.08.015; PMID 42691995. Preprint: 'Sexual dimorphism in the complete connectome of the Drosophila male central nervous system', bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.10.09.680999.
notes: live audit: Result text directly states that sex-specific and dimorphic neurons are concentrated in higher-order brain centers while the sensory and motor periphery is largely isomorphic. Final published counts: 166,700 neurons, 11,710 neuron types, and 8,069 isomorphic, 138 dimorphic, 289 male-specific and 71 female-specific types. Male-specific connections form 'hotspots', and dimorphic neurons reroute information. Author names (Berg, Beckett, Costa, Schlegel) were not visible in the results.

claims.claim: A male-female connectome comparison finds that vpoEN neurons have a strong sex-shared downstream partner (DNp55) and sex-specific partners (vpoDN in females, pC1_6a in males). This suggests the same auditory neuron type connects to different targets in each sex. Whether song activity actually flows this way in males has not been recorded.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, male CNS vs female (FlyWire) connectomes
claims.source_title: Sexual dimorphism in the complete Drosophila male central nervous system connectome
claims.source_authors: Janelia FlyEM, MRC LMB, Cambridge and Google Research consortium
notes: live audit: Result text states that vpoEN has a sex-shared downstream partner (DNp55) and sex-specific partners (vpoDN in females, pC1_6a in males). The male and female brains route the same sensory information via vpoEN to sex-specific downstream neurons through a 'switchboard motif'. The claim's caveat that this is wiring only, with no recording in males, is appropriate. For citation details, see T02-26.

claims.claim: The male CNS connectome identifies male-specific ascending neurons that carry information from nerve-cord song-generating neurons to brain song-detection circuits. The authors infer a closed loop in which the motor output of singing likely influences auditory detection of song.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, adult male (brain plus VNC connectome)
claims.source_title: Sexual dimorphism in the complete Drosophila male central nervous system connectome
claims.source_authors: Janelia FlyEM, MRC LMB, Cambridge and Google Research consortium
notes: live audit: The source exists and covers male song circuits across brain and VNC. However, no search result text explicitly described male-specific ascending neurons carrying song-generator information to brain song-detection circuits, or a closed motor-auditory loop. One aggregator summary mentioned a 'closed-loop system', but that was the search tool's own synthesis, not source text. Treat this as an inference by the authors that the results did not confirm.

claims.claim: A 2025 annotation of the female FlyWire brain connectome identified putative Fruitless and Doublesex neuron types by matching morphology to light-microscopy data (reported counts: 1,278 Fru, 50 Dsx, 79 ambiguous; unverified) and characterized their connectivity. SAG ascending neurons relaying post-mating (sex-peptide) information to pC1 was established earlier by functional work (Feng et al. 2014 Neuron; Wang F et al. 2020 Nature).
claims.source_title: Sexually-dimorphic neurons in the Drosophila whole-brain connectome
claims.source_authors: not confirmed in results
claims.corrected_citation: Sexually-dimorphic neurons in the Drosophila whole-brain connectome. bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.06.10.658788 (2025); also Research Square rs-6881911; PubMed 40661468; PMC12259084.
notes: live audit: Results describe this as the first comprehensive mapping of putative Fru and Dsx neurons in the female FlyWire connectome, found by matching LM to EM morphology: '91 Fru/Dsx types comprising over 1400 neurons'. That matches the claim's 1,278 + 50 + 79 = 1,407, but the per-category breakdown was not visible. Fru/Dsx neurons are highly interconnected yet receive most input from non-Fru/Dsx neurons, and labels are in FlyWire Codex. Authors were not visible in the results. The SAG-to-pC1 statement is cited to other work and was not checked here.

claims.claim: Laser Doppler vibrometry and acoustic measurements (likely Morley, Jonsson & Robert 2018, J Acoust Soc Am; confirm) report that the D. melanogaster antenna's mechanics are nonlinear. It is tuned near song frequencies at low amplitudes, and its resonance shifts up by hundreds of Hz at higher amplitudes. Song measured at the female during courtship was often louder than predicted, so under natural conditions the antenna may be operating outside its amplified, song-tuned regime.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster (biophysical measurement of antenna and song amplitude in courting pairs)
claims.source_title: Auditory sensitivity, spatial dynamics, and amplitude of courtship song in Drosophila melanogaster
claims.source_authors: not confirmed in results
notes: live audit: The title and PubMed entry are confirmed. Result text states that D. melanogaster audition is nonlinear, with the antenna tuned to song frequency at low amplitude and its resonance shifting up by hundreds of Hz as amplitude increases. The study quantified directional sensitivity and sender-receiver geometry. The finding that song at the female was louder than predicted was not visible. The author attribution (Morley, Jonsson & Robert) and the J Acoust Soc Am venue are still unconfirmed.

claims.claim: Female D. melanogaster respond to amplitude modulation within courtship song and prefer their own strain's song amplitude envelope over a flat or a steeper gain profile.
claims.source_title: Female Drosophila melanogaster respond to song-amplitude modulations
claims.source_authors: not confirmed in results
claims.corrected_citation: Brüggemeier B, Porter MA, Vigoreaux JO, Goodwin SF. Female Drosophila melanogaster respond to song-amplitude modulations. Biology Open 7(6):bio032003 (2018). PMID 29666051; PMC6031343.
notes: live audit: The authors are now identified. Result text: females 'prefer amplitude modulations that are typical of melanogaster song over other modulations'. The authors introduce the term 'song amplitude structure' (SAS). The specific comparison against flat and steeper gain profiles was not visible in the results.

new_leads_unverified.claim: The male CNS connectome shows that vPN1 is GABAergic. Its apparent excitation of pC1 in song processing is therefore disinhibitory: vPN1 inhibits a male-specific mAL, which inhibits pC1. This revises the aPN1 -> vPN1 -> pC1 excitatory chain proposed from 2015 imaging.
new_leads_unverified.source_title: Sexual dimorphism in the complete Drosophila male central nervous system connectome
new_leads_unverified.why_it_matters: It corrects the sign of a central link in the male song-perception pathway that track claims T02-10 and T02-11 rely on. Any model that uses connectome wiring to predict song responses needs the disinhibitory motif.

new_leads_unverified.claim: A 2025 Nature Communications paper describes a neural circuit for context-dependent multimodal signaling during Drosophila courtship. It appears to build on the pC2 song-detector/song-production work. Only the title was visible, so check the specific findings before using it.
new_leads_unverified.source_title: A neural circuit for context-dependent multimodal signaling in Drosophila
new_leads_unverified.why_it_matters: This is a recent circuit-level account of how flies choose between signal modalities by context. It is relevant to the two-way-communication framing and extends the pC2l results in T02-13.

claims.claim: Or67d ORNs (DA1 glomerulus) are required for the acute behavioral responses to cVA. Without Or67d, males court other males more and females are less receptive. Or65a ORNs, a second cVA-sensitive class, were later shown to carry the effects of long-term cVA exposure, so 'single class' applies only to acute responses.
claims.source_title: A single class of olfactory neurons mediates behavioural responses to a Drosophila sex pheromone
claims.source_authors: Kurtovic A, Widmer A, Dickson BJ
notes: live audit: Kurtovic, Widmer, Dickson, Nature 446:542-546 (2007) found. The result text says activating a single ORN class (Or67d) is necessary and sufficient for behavioural responses to cVA, which inhibits mating in males and promotes it in females. The Or65a caveat is supported separately by Liu et al. 2011 Nat Neurosci (https://www.nature.com/articles/nn.2836): chronic cVA reduces aggression through Or65a ORNs.

claims.claim: Or67d ORNs and DA1 PNs respond to cVA similarly in males and females (electrophysiology). However, the axon arbors of DA1 PNs in the lateral horn are sexually dimorphic and depend on fruitless (light-microscopy anatomy). This suggests the dimorphism lies in how DA1 PNs connect to third-order lateral horn neurons, not in how sensory neurons or PNs respond. Evidence type: anatomy (not a connectome) plus activity recordings that showed no sex difference.
claims.source_title: The Drosophila pheromone cVA activates a sexually dimorphic neural circuit
claims.source_authors: Datta SR, Vasconcelos ML, Ruta V, Luo S, Wong A, Demir E, Flores J, Balonze K, Dickson BJ, Axel R
claims.corrected_citation: Datta SR, Vasconcelos ML, Ruta V, Luo S, Wong A, Demir E, Flores J, Balonze K, Dickson BJ, Axel R (2008). The Drosophila pheromone cVA activates a sexually dimorphic neural circuit. Nature 452:473-477.
notes: live audit: Datta et al. 2008 Nature, 'The Drosophila pheromone cVA activates a sexually dimorphic neural circuit', appears in the results at the Nature URL. The detailed findings (no sex difference in ORN/PN responses, fru-dependent dimorphic LH arbors) were not in its snippet. Kohl et al. 2013's summary does state that first- and second-order olfactory neurons respond identically to cVA in both sexes, which indirectly supports the claim.

claims.claim: In males, a four-step cVA pathway was traced and recorded: Or67d ORN -> DA1 PN -> fru+ DC1 lateral horn neuron -> fru+ DN1 descending neuron. Electrophysiological recordings showed that DN1 responds to cVA, linking pheromone input to descending motor output.
claims.source_title: A dimorphic pheromone circuit in Drosophila from sensory input to descending output
claims.source_authors: Ruta V, Datta SR, Vasconcelos ML, Freeland J, Looger LL, Axel R
notes: live audit: Ruta, Datta, Vasconcelos, Freeland, Looger, Axel, Nature 468:686-690 (2010) found. The results state the circuit was traced from antennal sensory neurons to VNC descending neurons (PA-GFP tracing plus electrophysiology, imaging, microlesioning). It has at least four neurons and three synapses, three of the neurons are dimorphic, and a male-specific neuropil integrates multisensory input. The DC1/DN1 names and the DN1 cVA recording were not visible in the snippets.

claims.claim: cVA signals are sent to different sexually dimorphic lateral horn neuron classes in males and females (the aSP-f and aSP-g classes) through a fruitless-dependent 'bidirectional circuit switch'. In vivo whole-cell recordings combined with optogenetic stimulation of DA1 PNs showed sex-specific functional connectivity.
claims.source_title: A bidirectional circuit switch reroutes pheromone signals in male and female brains
claims.source_authors: Kohl J, Ostrovsky AD, Frechter S, Jefferis GSXE
notes: live audit: Kohl, Ostrovsky, Frechter, Jefferis, Cell 155(7):1610-1623 (2013) found. The result text says in vivo whole-cell recordings show two third-order LH clusters with dimorphic cVA responses (one responds in females, the other in males). Both clusters exist in both sexes and share input, and fruitless reroutes the input by setting dendrite position. The aSP-f/aSP-g labels and the DA1 PN optogenetics were not visible in the snippets.

claims.claim: Acute cVA exposure promotes male-male aggression through Or67d ORNs (Wang & Anderson 2010). Long-term exposure from group housing instead reduces aggression through Or65a ORNs (Liu et al. 2011). The same pheromone can therefore push aggression either way depending on timescale, while also suppressing male-male courtship.
