claims.source_title: Identification of an aggression-promoting pheromone and its receptor neurons in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Wang L, Anderson DJ
notes: live audit: Wang & Anderson, Nature 2010, found: cVA promotes male-male aggression through Or67d OSNs, and activating those OSNs is sufficient. Liu W, Liang X, Gong J et al., 'Social regulation of aggression by pheromonal activation of Or65a olfactory neurons in Drosophila', Nat Neurosci 14:896-902 (2011) (https://www.nature.com/articles/nn.2836), confirms the timescale point: acute cVA elicits aggression via Or67d, while chronic exposure or grouping reduces it via Or65a.

claims.claim: Combining the hemibrain/FlyWire connectomes with physiology, cVA processing splits in the lateral horn into parallel pathways. These represent the identity of the pheromone source and its position relative to the receiving fly.
claims.source_title: Generating parallel representations of position and identity in the olfactory system
claims.source_authors: Taisz I, Dona E, Munch D, ... Jefferis GSXE, Galili DS
notes: live audit: Taisz I, Dona E, Munch D, Bailey SN, Morris BJ, Meechan KI, Stevens KM, Varela-Martinez I, Gkantia M, Schlegel P, Ribeiro C, Jefferis GSXE, Galili DS, Cell 186(12):2556-2573.e22 (2023), found. The result text says a dedicated channel senses cVA and separate cVA-processing streams extract qualitative (identity) and positional information. The snippets did not show that the split happens specifically in the lateral horn or which connectome was used.

claims.claim: Foreleg ppk23+ gustatory neurons come in two functional subtypes. 'F-cells' respond to the female pheromone 7,11-HD and 'M-cells' respond to male pheromones (e.g., 7-T), as shown by calcium imaging. ppk23 neurons are needed for normal male courtship of females and for male-male courtship repulsion.
claims.source_title: Contact chemoreceptors mediate male-male repulsion and male-female attraction during Drosophila courtship
claims.source_authors: Thistle R, Cameron P, Ghorayshi A, Dennison L, Scott K (also Toda H, Zhao X, Dickson BJ 2012 Cell Reports; Lu B et al. 2012 PLoS Genet)
notes: live audit: Thistle, Cameron, Ghorayshi, Dennison, Scott, Cell 149(5):1140-1151 (2012) found. The results say ppk23 and ppk29 are expressed in fru+ foreleg neurons that are necessary and sufficient to inhibit courtship toward males and promote it toward females, with different cells responding selectively to male or female pheromones. The paper involves ppk29 as well as ppk23.

claims.claim: Calcium imaging of P1 in males during foreleg pheromone stimulation shows that female contact pheromones excite P1 and the male pheromone 7-T inhibits it, a balance that biases mate choice (Kallman et al. 2015). Kallman et al. identified PPN1 relay neurons, and Clowney et al. 2015 identified vAB3 excitation and mAL inhibition. Exactly how 7-T -> PPN1 -> mAL -> P1 connect needs to be confirmed from the primary paper.
claims.source_title: Excitation and inhibition onto central courtship neurons biases Drosophila mate choice
claims.source_authors: Kallman BR, Kim H, Scott K
notes: live audit: Kallman, Kim, Scott, eLife 4:e11188 (2015) found. The eLife digest text says female pheromones activate a pathway that excites P1 and male pheromones activate a pathway that inhibits P1, shown with functional imaging, optogenetics, anatomy and behaviour. The PPN1 relay and the exact 7-T -> PPN1 -> mAL -> P1 wiring were not visible in the results, so the claim's own caveat stands.

claims.claim: P1 neurons act as a multisensory integrator in the male brain. They are excited by female contact pheromones via vAB3 and gated by feedforward inhibition via mAL, and the volatile pheromone cVA suppresses P1 excitation. This was shown with calcium imaging and electrophysiology in ex vivo and in vivo preparations with foreleg stimulation.
claims.source_title: Multimodal chemosensory circuits controlling male courtship in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Clowney EJ, Iguchi S, Bussell JJ, Scheer E, Ruta V
notes: live audit: Clowney, Iguchi, Bussell, Scheer, Ruta, Neuron 87(5):1036-1049 (2015) found. The result text confirms only that courtship is triggered by activating dimorphic P1 interneurons. The specific vAB3 excitation, mAL feedforward inhibition and cVA suppression of P1 were not visible in the snippets.

claims.claim: In males, dTrpA1 activation of fruitless-expressing neurons induced courtship acts, and courtship initiation correlated with activation of P1 interneurons, descending P2b neurons, or both (mosaic analysis). Female contact evoked activity in P1 in tethered males.
claims.source_title: Female contact activates male-specific interneurons that trigger stereotypic courtship behavior in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Kohatsu S, Koganezawa M, Yamamoto D
claims.corrected_citation: Kohatsu S, Koganezawa M, Yamamoto D (2011). Female contact activates male-specific interneurons that trigger stereotypic courtship behavior in Drosophila. Neuron 69(3):498-508.
notes: live audit: The source is confirmed. The result summary says the causal evidence comes from dTrpA1 activation of fru+ neurons, with initiation correlated with P1 and/or P2b activation. It was not a P1-specific activation, so 'activating P1 triggered courtship' overstates it. The foreleg-contact calcium result fits the title, but the snippets did not describe it.

claims.claim: In D. simulans, 7,11-HD (a female pheromone of D. melanogaster) suppresses male courtship. Peripheral detection by ppk23+ neurons is conserved, but the central route to P1 differs. In D. melanogaster, 7,11-HD excites P1 via vAB3. In D. simulans, the balance shifts toward inhibition via the GABAergic mAL pathway, so P1 is not activated. This was shown by calcium imaging in both species. Whether PPN1 is part of the altered pathway is unconfirmed.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster vs D. simulans, males
claims.source_title: Evolution of a central neural circuit underlies Drosophila mate preferences
claims.source_authors: Seeholzer LF, Seppo M, Stern DL, Ruta V
notes: live audit: Seeholzer, Seppo, Stern, Ruta, Nature 2018 found. The result text says 7,11-HD promotes courtship in D. melanogaster males but suppresses it in D. simulans males. Both species detect it with homologous peripheral neurons, but the signal reaches P1 differently, so the change is central. The vAB3/mAL mechanism is mentioned only as neurons involved; the direction of the excitation/inhibition balance was not visible.

claims.claim: Gr32a-expressing gustatory neurons are required for 7-T to promote male aggression and for normal suppression of male-male courtship. Whether Gr32a neurons themselves detect 7-T is disputed, since ppk23+ M cells also respond to 7-T. Contact chemosensation still sits upstream of the fight-or-court decision.
claims.source_title: Hierarchical chemosensory regulation of male-male social interactions in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Wang L, Han X, Mehren J, Hiroi M, Billeter JC, Miyamoto T, Amrein H, Levine JD, Anderson DJ (see also Miyamoto T, Amrein H 2008 Nat Neurosci)
notes: live audit: Wang L et al., Nature Neuroscience 2011, found. The results say (Z)-7-tricosene is essential for normal aggression, and its aggression-promoting and courtship-suppressing effects are independent but both need Gr32a. 7-T sensitivity is also needed for cVA's aggression effect, which is the 'hierarchical' regulation. The dispute over whether Gr32a neurons detect 7-T directly was not addressed in the results.

claims.claim: LC10a lobula columnar visual projection neurons are needed for a courting male to track the female and to orient his unilateral wing extension toward her. Silencing LC10a impairs visual pursuit during courtship.
claims.source_title: Visual projection neurons mediating directed courtship in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Ribeiro IMA, Drews M, Bahl A, Machacek C, Borst A, Dickson BJ
notes: live audit: Ribeiro IMA, Drews M, Bahl A, Machacek C, Borst A, Dickson BJ, Cell 174(3):607-621 (2018) found. The results say males with LC10 silenced cannot orient toward or stay near the female and do not mainly use the ipsilateral wing. LC10 neurons respond to small moving objects, and LC10a is the subtype described. The results phrase the silencing at the LC10 level.

claims.claim: Sexual arousal (P1 activity) gates visual processing during courtship. With two-photon imaging in tethered males pursuing a visual target, visual signals from the LC10a pathway drove pursuit only when males were aroused, and optogenetic P1 activation made males pursue a moving target.
claims.source_title: Sexual arousal gates visual processing during Drosophila courtship
claims.source_authors: Hindmarsh Sten T, Li R, Otopalik A, Ruta V
notes: live audit: Hindmarsh Sten T, Li R, Otopalik A, Ruta V, Nature 595:549-553 (2021) found. The results say LC10a activity rises when males are sexually aroused and that LC10a activation triggers robust courtship only in that state, with P1 setting arousal. The bioRxiv preprint was titled 'An arousal-gated visual circuit controls pursuit during Drosophila courtship'.

claims.claim: A deep network trained with 'knockout training' on male courtship behavior mapped model units onto LC visual projection neuron types. It predicted that female features (position, size, heading) are carried by a combinatorial population code across many LC types, not by single dedicated channels. The prediction was tested against LC neuron imaging.
claims.source_title: Mapping model units to visual neurons reveals population code for social behaviour
claims.source_authors: Cowley BR, Calhoun AJ, Rangarajan N, ... Pillow JW, Murthy M
claims.corrected_citation: Cowley BR, Calhoun AJ, Rangarajan N, Ireland E, Turner MH, Pillow JW, Murthy M (2024). Mapping model units to visual neurons reveals population code for social behaviour. Nature 629:1100-1108.
notes: live audit: The source is confirmed, including the 'knockout training' method (perturbing the network in training to match neuronal perturbations of more than a dozen cell types) in male visually guided courtship. The title states the population-code conclusion. The full author list is Cowley, Calhoun, Rangarajan, Ireland, Turner, Pillow, Murthy.

claims.claim: Courting males make abdominal quivering movements that send substrate-borne vibrations. Females respond by becoming immobile (stopping), which helps copulation. Playing artificial vibrations reproduces the female stopping response.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, male sender / female receiver
claims.source_title: Substrate-borne vibratory communication during courtship in Drosophila melanogaster
claims.source_authors: Fabre CCG, Hedwig B, Conduit G, Lawrence PA, Goodwin SF, Casal J
notes: live audit: Fabre CCG, Hedwig B, Conduit G, Lawrence PA, Goodwin SF, Casal J, Current Biology (Nov 2012) found. The results say male abdominal quivering at 4-6 Hz sends substrate-borne vibrations that coincide and correlate strongly with female immobility, which helps copulation. The artificial-vibration playback reproducing female stopping was not visible in the snippets. A follow-up, 'Drosophila females receive male substrate-borne signals through specific leg neurons during courtship' (Current Biology 2021, PubMed 34174209), identifies the female receptor neurons.

claims.claim: In virgin females, dsx+ pC1 neurons respond to cVA and courtship song in calcium imaging, and their activity bidirectionally controls receptivity (Zhou et al. 2014). pC1 is heterogeneous, however: later work assigns receptivity and mating status mainly to pC1a and related subtypes, and aggression/persistent state to pC1d/pC1e.
claims.source_title: Central brain neurons expressing doublesex regulate female receptivity in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Zhou C, Pan Y, Robinett CC, Meissner GW, Baker BS
notes: live audit: Zhou, Pan, Robinett, Meissner, Baker, Neuron (July 2014) found. The results say activating pC1 or pCd promotes receptivity and silencing either makes females unreceptive. Both respond to cVA, and pC1 also responds to courtship song. The claim leaves out that pCd shares the cVA response and the receptivity role. The later pC1 subtype assignments were not checked here.

claims.claim: The post-mating switch requires SPR in a small set of fru+/ppk+ (also dsx+) sensory neurons of the female reproductive tract, later called SPSNs. Silencing these neurons in virgins mimics the mated state (lower receptivity, more egg laying). This led to the model that sex peptide acts by reducing their activity; the 2008-2009 papers inferred this silencing rather than recording it directly.
claims.source_title: A receptor that mediates the post-mating switch in Drosophila reproductive behaviour; Sensory neurons in the Drosophila genital tract regulate female reproductive behavior
claims.source_authors: Yapici N, Kim YJ, Ribeiro C, Dickson BJ (2008); Hasemeyer M, Yapici N, Heberlein U, Dickson BJ (2009); also Yang CH et al. (2009) Neuron
claims.corrected_citation: Yapici N, Kim YJ, Ribeiro C, Dickson BJ (2008) Nature; Häsemeyer M, Yapici N, Heberlein U, Dickson BJ (2009) Neuron; Yang CH, Rumpf S, Xiang Y, Gordon MD, Song W, Jan LY, Jan YN (2009) Control of the postmating behavioral switch in Drosophila females by internal sensory neurons. Neuron.
notes: live audit: Yapici N, Kim YJ, Ribeiro C, Dickson BJ, Nature 451:33-37 (2008) (https://www.nature.com/articles/nature06483) and Hasemeyer M, Yapici N, Heberlein U, Dickson BJ, Neuron 61:511-518 (2009) found. SPR is needed for the post-mating switch, and SPR in a small set of fru+/ppk+ uterine and oviduct sensory neurons is necessary and sufficient. The Wang F et al. 2020 Nature summary states that sex peptide silences these neurons and their ascending targets, which fits the silencing model. Yang CH et al. 2009 Neuron was not separately searched.

claims.claim: SAG ascending neurons in the abdominal ganglion receive SPSN input and carry mating-status information to the central brain. Silencing SAG makes virgin females less receptive and raises egg laying, mimicking the mated state. The downstream SAG-to-pC1 connection was established later by EM connectomics (Wang F et al. 2020).
claims.source_title: Ascending SAG neurons control sexual receptivity of Drosophila females
claims.source_authors: Feng K, Palfreyman MT, Hasemeyer M, Talsma A, Dickson BJ
claims.corrected_citation: Feng K, Palfreyman MT, Häsemeyer M, Talsma A, Dickson BJ (2014) Neuron 83. For SAG->pC1 wiring: Wang F, Wang K, Forknall N, Patrick C, Yang T, Parekh R, Bock D, Dickson BJ (2020) Nature.
notes: live audit: Feng K, Palfreyman MT, Hasemeyer M, Talsma A, Dickson BJ, Neuron 83(1):135-148 (2014) found. The results say SAG neurons get synaptic input from sensory neurons in the abdominal ganglion and project to the dorsal protocerebrum. Silencing SAG makes virgins unreceptive, and activating SAG raises receptivity in mated females. The egg-laying effect of SAG silencing was not visible in the snippets. The SPSN -> SAG -> pC1 three-tier circuit is supported by the Wang F et al. 2020 Nature summary.

claims.claim: oviDNs are command-like descending neurons for egg laying. They receive excitatory (oviEN) and inhibitory (oviIN) inputs, and pC1 neurons, which carry mating-status input from SAG, feed into this circuit. This is the egg-laying circuit, not the ovipositor-extrusion rejection circuit. Evidence: causal manipulations plus EM connectivity (FAFB and/or hemibrain; dataset to be confirmed).
claims.source_title: Neural circuitry linking mating and egg laying in Drosophila females
claims.source_authors: Wang F, Wang K, Forknall N, Patrick C, Yang T, Parekh R, Bock D, Dickson BJ
notes: live audit: Wang F, Wang K, Forknall N, Patrick C, Yang T, Parekh R, Bock D, Dickson BJ, Nature 579(7797):101-105 (2020) found. The results say activating the female-specific oviDNs is necessary and sufficient for egg laying and works equally well in virgin and mated females. Sex peptide silences uterine sensory neurons and their ascending (SAG) targets, forming an SPSN-SAG-pC1 circuit. The oviEN/oviIN identities and the EM dataset (probably FAFB, given Bock is an author) were not visible in the snippets.

claims.claim: DNp13 descending neurons are command-type neurons for ovipositor extrusion (OE), and OE deters males only when mated females perform it. DNp13 respond to male song through direct synaptic input from pC2l auditory neurons. Mating status does not change DNp13 song responses; it changes how well DNp13 engage the OE motor circuits. That status signal comes from ppk+ uterine sensory neurons that are activated at ovulation. Vaginal plate opening and OE are controlled by anatomically and functionally distinct circuits.
claims.source_title: Circuit and behavioral mechanisms of sexual rejection by Drosophila females
claims.source_authors: Wang F, Wang K, Forknall N, Parekh R, Dickson BJ
notes: live audit: The source is confirmed (Current Biology 2020). The results name the missing pieces: the song input to DNp13 is direct from pC2l, and mating status acts downstream of DNp13's song responses via ppk+ uterine sensory neurons activated at ovulation. It is not described as coming through pC1, so the 'possibly via pC1' speculation should be dropped.

claims.claim: Vaginal plate opening (VPO), the virgin female's acceptance signal, is controlled by a pair of female-specific descending neurons (vpoDNs). vpoDNs receive excitatory input from auditory vpoEN neurons tuned to specific features of D. melanogaster courtship song, and from pC1 neurons that encode the female's mating status.
claims.source_title: Neural circuit mechanisms of sexual receptivity in Drosophila females
claims.source_authors: Wang K, Wang F, Forknall N, Yang T, Patrick C, Parekh R, Dickson BJ
claims.corrected_citation: Wang K, Wang F, Forknall N, Yang T, Patrick C, Parekh R, Dickson BJ (2021). Neural circuit mechanisms of sexual receptivity in Drosophila females. Nature 589(7843):577-581. (bioRxiv 10.1101/2020.08.07.241919)
notes: live audit: The venue is wrong: the paper is in Nature (589:577-581, 2021), not Neuron (FlyBase FBrf0247919 confirms). The core content is confirmed. The results did not show 'pulse song' specifically (they say 'specific features of D. melanogaster song'), pC1 carrying male pheromone cues, or which EM dataset was used.

claims.claim: In virgin females, ovipositor extrusion signals ACCEPTANCE. It prompts males to attempt copulation and helps the transition from courtship to copulation, unlike the rejection role of extrusion in mated females.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, virgin females and males
claims.source_title: Ovipositor extrusion promotes the transition from courtship to copulation and signals female acceptance in Drosophila melanogaster
claims.source_authors: Mezzera C, Brotas M, Gaspar M, ... Vasconcelos ML
claims.corrected_citation: Mezzera C, Brotas M, Gaspar M, Pavlou HJ, Goodwin SF, Vasconcelos ML (2020). Ovipositor extrusion promotes the transition from courtship to copulation and signals female acceptance in Drosophila melanogaster. Current Biology 30(19):3736-3748.e5.
notes: live audit: The source is confirmed, and the title states the claim. The results say that when the male licks an extruded ovipositor, he attempts copulation, and that the ovipositor has a dual function. One aggregator summary also mentions ovipositor retraction in acceptance, so the fine-grained 'extrusion vs retraction' wording should be checked against the abstract.

claims.claim: In females, optogenetic activation of pC1d/pC1e neurons triggers a persistent internal state lasting minutes that raises female aggression. Imaging showed long-lasting activity. EM reconstruction in the FAFB volume via FlyWire (the hemibrain may have been used for comparison) revealed recurrent connectivity among pC1d, pC1e and aIPg that could hold that state.
claims.source_title: The neural basis for a persistent internal state in Drosophila females
claims.source_authors: Deutsch D, Pacheco D, Encarnacion-Rivera L, Pereira T, Fathy R, Clemens J, Girardin C, Calhoun A, Ireland E, Burke A, Dorkenwald S, McKellar C, Macrina T, Lu R, Lee K, Kemnitz N, Ih D, Castro M, Halageri A, Jordan C, Silversmith W, Wu J, Seung HS, Murthy M

The neural basis for a persistent internal state in Drosophila females. eLife. (EM data: FAFB via FlyWire.)
notes: live audit: Deutsch et al., eLife 2020, found. The results say pC1d/e drive minutes-long changes in female behaviour when males are present, and connectome mapping of all pC1d/pC1e inputs and outputs shows strong recurrent connectivity with fru+ aIPg neurons. Caveat: Schretter et al. 2020 found that activating pC1d alone gave only time-locked aggression and pC1e had no effect, while aIPg stimulation gave aggression outlasting the stimulus. Which node holds the persistent aggressive state is refined in a later eLife paper, 'Cell type-specific contributions to a persistent aggressive internal state in female Drosophila' (https://elifesciences.org/articles/88598). The FAFB/FlyWire dataset was not visible in the snippets.

claims.claim: aIPg neurons, downstream of pC1d, drive female aggression (head-butting, shoving). Split-GAL4 lines plus hemibrain connectivity defined the cell types in the female aggression circuit.
claims.source_title: Cell types and neuronal circuitry underlying female aggression in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Schretter CE, Aso Y, Robie AA, Dreher M, Dolan MJ, Chen N, Ito M, Yang T, Parekh R, Branson KM, Rubin GM
notes: live audit: Schretter et al., eLife 2020, found. The results say the paper identified aIPg as a female aggression-promoting cell type, that 30 s of aIPg stimulation caused aggression outlasting the stimulus, and that pC1d activation alone gave time-locked aggression. This fits aIPg acting downstream of or recurrent with pC1d.

claims.claim: Activating P1 neurons in males produces a persistent internal state that raises male-male aggression, lasting minutes after stimulation ends. So P1 is an arousal/state hub, not just a courtship 'command' neuron.
claims.source_title: P1 interneurons promote a persistent internal state that enhances inter-male aggression
claims.source_authors: Hoopfer ED, Jung Y, Inagaki HK, Rubin GM, Anderson DJ (see also Jung Y et al. 2020 Neuron on P1a)
notes: live audit: The eLife 2015 article appears in the results under the exact title 'P1 interneurons promote a persistent internal state that enhances inter-male aggression in Drosophila', and the title states the key finding. The author list (Hoopfer, Jung, Inagaki, Rubin, Anderson) was not shown in the result, and Jung et al. 2020 was not searched.

claims.claim: Males pattern their song in real time using feedback cues from the female. The choice between pulse and sine song depends on male-female distance and female speed (Coen et al. 2014). Song amplitude is adjusted to distance (Coen et al. 2016). Visual cues contribute, but vision was not shown to be the sole or main channel.
claims.source_title: Dynamic sensory cues shape song structure in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Coen P, Clemens J, Weinstein AJ, Pacheco DA, Deng Y, Murthy M
claims.corrected_citation: Coen P, Clemens J, Weinstein AJ, Pacheco DA, Deng Y, Murthy M (2014) Nature; plus Coen P, Xie M, Clemens J, Murthy M (2016) Sensorimotor transformations underlying variability in song intensity during Drosophila courtship. Neuron.
notes: live audit: Coen P, Clemens J, Weinstein AJ et al., Nature 507:233-237 (2014) found. The result summary says males pattern song according to visual and self-motion sensory inputs, comparing song when near versus far from the female, and that females change walking speed in response. This fits the claim, including the hedge that vision is not the only input. Coen et al. 2016 Neuron (song amplitude vs distance) was not searched.

claims.claim: In females, ppk25-expressing pheromone-sensing neurons promote receptivity to male courtship. The same channel subunit also supports male courtship, so contact chemosensation matters on the female side too.
claims.source_title: Drosophila pheromone-sensing neurons expressing the ppk25 ion channel subunit stimulate male courtship and female receptivity
claims.source_authors: Vijayan V, Thistle R, Liu T, Starostina E, Pikielny CW
notes: live audit: Vijayan, Thistle, Liu, Starostina, Pikielny, PLoS Genetics 10(3):e1004238 (2014) found. The results say ppk25 works in neurons that detect female pheromones and drive male courtship, and that in both males and females these neurons specifically stimulate courtship and mating (female receptivity).

claims.claim: FlyWire (a single adult female brain, about 139k neurons, hemibrain-matched cell types) lets researchers trace brain-level social inputs, including LC visual neurons, DA1 pheromone PNs and the brain axons of ascending neurons, to the female pC1 cluster and descending neurons. It is wiring only. It lacks the nerve cord and leg sensory neurons, so full contact-pheromone paths need BANC or male-CNS data, and male-specific circuits such as P1 are absent.
claims.source_title: Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain; Whole-brain annotation and multi-connectome cell typing of Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Dorkenwald S et al.; Schlegel P et al. (FlyWire Consortium)
claims.corrected_citation: Dorkenwald S et al. (2024). Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain. Nature (PubMed 37425937). Schlegel P et al. (2024). Whole-brain annotation and multi-connectome cell typing quantifies circuit stereotypy in Drosophila. Nature.
notes: live audit: Both FlyWire papers were confirmed as Nature 2024. The dataset is 139,255 proofread neurons and about 5x10^7 synapses from one adult female brain. The Schlegel title in the claim is truncated; the full title ends '...quantifies circuit stereotypy in Drosophila'. The limitation and the pointer to BANC are supported: BANC (Nature 2026, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10735-w) is a single adult female brain plus nerve-cord connectome. FlyWire-based dimorphism work also exists ('Sexually-dimorphic neurons in the Drosophila whole-brain connectome').

claims.claim: The complete male CNS connectome (brain plus nerve cord, one animal; about 166,700 neurons and 11,710 neuron types, fully proofread and annotated for fruitless/doublesex expression) was compared with the female FlyWire brain at synaptic resolution. It found 8,069 isomorphic, 138 dimorphic, 289 male-specific and 71 female-specific types. Sex-specific or dimorphic neurons make up 4.8% of male and 2.4% of female central-brain neurons. They cluster in higher-order centres while the sensory and motor periphery is largely isomorphic, and dimorphism spreads through dimorphic connectivity. Dimorphism status matches fru/dsx expression closely but not perfectly.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, adult male (single CNS) vs female
claims.source_title: Sexual dimorphism in the complete connectome of the Drosophila male central nervous system
claims.source_authors: Berg S, Beckett IR, Costa M, Schlegel P, ... Jefferis GSXE and collaborators (Janelia FlyEM / Cambridge)
claims.venue: bioRxiv preprint 2025; Cell (Sept 2026, per program context)
claims.corrected_citation: [Berg S, Beckett IR, Costa M, Schlegel P, ... Jefferis GSXE et al.; author list not visible in search results] (2026). Sexual dimorphism in the complete Drosophila male central nervous system connectome. Cell (PII S0092-8674(26)00942-6; PubMed 42691995). Preprint: 'Sexual dimorphism in the complete connectome of the Drosophila male central nervous system', bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.10.09.680999 (Oct 2025).

The Cell 2026 journal version exists (Cell/ScienceDirect/PubMed listings), and its title differs from the preprint's ('...complete Drosophila male central nervous system connectome'). Authors were not visible in the results. The specific P1-vs-pC1 hub comparison was not shown in the snippets. Janelia project page: https://www.janelia.org/project-team/flyem/male-cns-connectome

new_leads_unverified.claim: A connectome of the brain and ventral nerve cord of a single adult female fly (BANC) was reconstructed and annotated as an open resource. It shows neural control of behaviour to be distributed, parallel and embodied, and allows sensory-to-motor tracing across the neck connective, which FlyWire lacks.
new_leads_unverified.source_title: Distributed control circuits across a brain-and-cord connectome
new_leads_unverified.why_it_matters: Fills the FlyWire gap noted in T03-29. Female leg contact-chemosensory and substrate-vibration inputs can be traced to pC1, vpoDN and DNp13 in one animal.

new_leads_unverified.claim: A complete connectomic description of Drosophila ascending and descending neurons, integrating three EM datasets with cell types matched across hemispheres, datasets and sexes. It includes an analysis of stereotypy and sexual dimorphism, and 51% of DN types are matched to driver lines.
new_leads_unverified.source_title: Comparative connectomics of Drosophila descending and ascending neurons
new_leads_unverified.why_it_matters: Gives the cross-sex DN/AN map needed to compare output channels (oviDN, vpoDN, DNp13, P1-driven DNs) and ascending status signals such as SAG.

new_leads_unverified.claim: The same brain neurons that drive male courtship song also control substrate-borne vibrations through separate premotor pathways with cell-type-specific dynamics, so one command signal is routed to two communication channels depending on context.
new_leads_unverified.source_title: A neural circuit for context-dependent multimodal signaling in Drosophila
new_leads_unverified.why_it_matters: Links the vibration channel (T03-16) and the song channel (T03-27) at the circuit level, which matters for designing multimodal playback.

new_leads_unverified.claim: The male CNS connectome annotates sensory neurons and reports higher sensory neuron numbers in males, which may help them sustain pheromone responses during prolonged courtship exposure.
new_leads_unverified.source_title: Sexual dimorphism in the complete connectome of the Drosophila male central nervous system (bioRxiv preprint; Cell 2026 version)
new_leads_unverified.why_it_matters: Primary resource for synapse-level P1 and pC1 comparison. The preprint and journal titles differ, which matters for citation.

new_leads_unverified.claim: Cryo-EM structures of the Or67d-Orco receptor complex reveal the structural mechanism of insect pheromone (cVA) sensing.
new_leads_unverified.source_title: Cryo-EM structures of Drosophila OR67d-Orco complexes reveal insect pheromone sensing mechanism
new_leads_unverified.why_it_matters: Gives the molecular basis of the cVA channel at the start of T03-01 to T03-06, which is useful for designing synthetic agonists as 'words' in a two-way signalling system.

new_leads_unverified.claim: Male cuticular pheromones stimulate mated females to remove the mating plug and promote re-mating, acting through pC1 neurons.
new_leads_unverified.source_title: Male cuticular pheromones stimulate removal of the mating plug and promote re-mating through pC1 neurons in Drosophila females
new_leads_unverified.why_it_matters: Extends the pC1 hub (T03-17, T03-19, T03-22) to a post-mating reply channel and shows that contact pheromone signals can reverse the mated-state switch.

claims.claim: In freely walking, socially interacting male D. melanogaster, ratiometric imaging through a head window (Flyception2) showed fruitless-expressing P1 neurons active during courtship but inactive during copulation, while GABAergic mAL neurons stayed active during copulation.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, adult male, freely moving (head cuticle window, retroreflective-marker tracking)
claims.source_title: Imaging brain activity during complex social behaviors in Drosophila with Flyception2
claims.source_authors: Grover D, Katsuki T, Li J, Dawkins TJ, Greenspan RJ
notes: live audit: Title, venue (Nature Communications 2020) and topic match. The result text directly says Flyception2 uses retroreflective-marker tracking plus ratiometric imaging in copulating males, and that P1 neurons are active during courtship but inactive during copulation while GABAergic mAL neurons remain active during copulation. PMC mirror: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6992788/

claims.claim: In tethered males courting a moving dot in virtual reality, P1 activity tracks moment-to-moment pursuit intensity, and the gain of LC10a visual projection neurons is selectively raised during courtship.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, adult male, head-fixed on air-supported ball
claims.source_title: Sexual arousal gates visual processing during Drosophila courtship
claims.source_authors: Hindmarsh Sten T, Li R, Otopalik A, Ruta V
notes: live audit: Not searched directly. The T04-31 search (Rockefeller news) confirms the Ruta lab study was published in Nature (not Cell), used a tethered male on an air-supported ball chasing a projected moving dot, and found P1 neurons act as an arousal switch that reroutes visual information. P1 tracking pursuit intensity and the LC10a gain increase were not visible in the results. Nature primary URL not seen in results.

claims.claim: Calcium imaging of the ventral nerve cord during singing showed nested song-motor populations: dPR1 neurons are selectively active during pulse song, while TN1A neurons are active during both pulse and sine song.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, adult male, two-photon imaging during song (exact prep/elicitation not confirmed in snippets)
claims.source_title: Activity of nested neural circuits drives different courtship songs in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Shiozaki HM, Wang K, Lillvis JL, Xu M, Dickson BJ, Stern DL
notes: live audit: Nature Neuroscience, August 2024 (PubMed 39198658) matches. The result directly states that VNC calcium imaging in singing flies found one population active during both songs and an expanded population, including the first, active during pulse song. The results do not name the cells in the Nat Neurosci abstract. The companion Lillvis et al. 2024 Current Biology summary puts TN1A in the sine (smaller) circuit and dPR1 in the expanded pulse circuit, which fits the claim's dPR1 = pulse-selective, TN1A = both. PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39198658/

claims.claim: Brain recordings showed the same nested activation in the two descending pathways needed for song (pIP10 and pMP2), and connectome analysis showed these pathways give structured input to VNC song neurons consistent with that pattern.
claims.source_title: Activity of nested neural circuits drives different courtship songs in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Shiozaki HM et al.
notes: live audit: The result text directly states: 'Brain recordings showed that this nested activation pattern is present in two descending pathways required for singing'. A second search summary adds that connectomic analysis shows the pIP10 and pMP2 descending pathways give structured input to VNC neurons. Both parts of the claim are supported.

claims.claim: Optogenetic activation of the descending neuron pIP10 induces both pulse and sine song, whereas pMP2 activation induces pulse but not sine song.
claims.source_title: Activity of nested neural circuits drives different courtship songs in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Shiozaki HM et al.
notes: live audit: The search result text for this paper states verbatim that optogenetic activation of pIP10 induces both pulse and sine song, whereas pMP2 activation induces pulse but not sine song. The paper also activated dPR1 and TN1A-2 during natural courtship.

claims.claim: Lillvis et al. (2024, Curr Biol 34:808-824) built split-GAL4 lines for VNC song-circuit cell types and scored song automatically (reported as SongExplorer, which separates pulse from sine). With activation and silencing they showed that pulse and sine song come from nested neural circuits. The exact counts (58 lines, at least 40 cell types) still need checking against the paper.
claims.source_title: Nested neural circuits generate distinct acoustic signals during Drosophila courtship
claims.source_authors: Lillvis JL, Wang K, Shiozaki HM, Xu M, Stern DL, Dickson BJ
claims.corrected_citation: Lillvis JL, et al. Nested neural circuits generate distinct acoustic signals during Drosophila courtship. Curr Biol 2024;34(4):808-824.e6 (published online 30 Jan 2024).
notes: live audit: Search results directly state the 58 lines and at least 40 cell types, optogenetic silencing and activation with GtACR1, and the nested feed-forward organization with pulse song produced by the larger network. FlyBase confirms Curr Biol 34(4):808-824.e6. The 'still need checking' hedge can be dropped. SongExplorer as the scoring tool was not visible in the results.

claims.claim: Two-photon imaging of TN1 wing-motor neurons during optogenetic pIP10 drive: nearly half were positively correlated with the stimulus, while a smaller fraction were anti-correlated, with alternating peaks that persisted after stimulation. Behaviorally, males sang simple one-mode trains far from the female and alternating sequences near her.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, adult male (imaging under optogenetic drive, not natural singing)
claims.source_title: Flexible circuit mechanisms for context-dependent song sequencing
claims.source_authors: Roemschied FA, Pacheco DA, Aragon MJ, Ireland EC, Li X, Thieringer K, Pang R, Murthy M
notes: live audit: Citation confirmed: Roemschied FA, Pacheco DA, Aragon MJ, Ireland EC, Li X, Thieringer K, Pang R, Murthy M. Nature 622:794-801 (Oct 2023). Results directly state simple one-mode trains far from the female and alternating sequences near her, VNC mutual inhibition and rebound excitability, and csChrimson in pIP10 and TN1. The fractions of TN1 neurons correlated or anti-correlated with the stimulus were not visible.

claims.claim: Whole-central-brain volumetric imaging with cross-brain registration found auditory activity in most central-brain regions, with most of it tuned to courtship-song features. Responses were stereotyped in early mechanosensory regions and more variable in higher regions, and this variability was largely independent of ongoing movement.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, adult males and females, head-fixed
claims.source_title: Auditory activity is diverse and widespread throughout the central brain of Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Pacheco DA, Thiberge SY, Pnevmatikakis E, Murthy M
notes: live audit: Citation confirmed: Pacheco DA, Thiberge SY, Pnevmatikakis E et al., Nat Neurosci 24:93-104 (2021); FlyBase also lists 24(1):93-104. The result directly states the volumetric imaging with across-brain registration, auditory activity in most central-brain regions, temporally diverse responses, and a majority tuned to courtship-song features. The second half of the claim (stereotyped responses in early mechanosensory regions, more variable in higher regions, variability largely independent of movement) was not visible in the snippets. It agrees with the verifier's memory of the abstract.

claims.claim: Light beads microscopy recorded brain-wide calcium signals in behaving adult flies at 28 volumes/s (60 volumes/s for the central brain alone). It revealed fast auditory responses that standard volumetric two-photon imaging misses, and temporal super-resolution recovered responses to single courtship-song pulses.
claims.source_title: High-speed whole-brain imaging in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Gauthey et al.
notes: live audit: Gauthey et al., 'High-speed whole-brain imaging in Drosophila', Nature Communications (2026), from bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.06.18.660371; PubMed 40611904 and a PMC record exist. Results directly state LBM in behaving adult flies at 28 volumes/s (60 volumes/s for central brain only), fast auditory responses missed by standard volumetric imaging, and temporal super-resolution recovering responses to single song pulses. The article number 17:5810 was not visible in the results.

claims.claim: Dsx+ pC2 neurons (pC2l and pC2m) are tuned to several temporal features of pulse song, with similar tuning in males and females. This comes from two-photon imaging of pC2 cell bodies and of Dsx+ neurites in the lateral junction (LJ), a neuropil region, not a cell type. Optogenetic pC2 activation drives sex-specific behaviours, including song production in males.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, adult males and females
claims.source_title: Shared Song Detector Neurons in Drosophila Male and Female Brains Drive Sex-Specific Behaviors
claims.source_authors: Deutsch D, Clemens J, Thiberge SY, Guan G, Murthy M
notes: live audit: Citation confirmed: Deutsch D, Clemens J, Thiberge SY, Guan G, Murthy M, Current Biology, October 2019. The results state that Dsx+ pC2 neurons are tuned to multiple temporal aspects of pulse song and drive sex-specific behaviours, that pC2 splits into pC2l and pC2m which both project to the lateral junction, and that males and females had similar (behavioural) tuning for pulse song. Minor precision issue: the activation experiments used a pC2l-specific driver (CsChrimson), so 'pC2l activation' is more exact than 'pC2 activation'. A 2023 Current Biology item with the same title also exists (cell.com S0960-9822(23)01049-7), probably a correction notice, and should be checked. PMC: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6885007/

claims.claim: In virgin females, the female-specific descending neurons vpoDN showed strong calcium rises in soma and neurites during playback of male courtship song (GCaMP6s, two-photon). They receive excitatory input from song-tuned vpoEN auditory neurons and from pC1.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, adult virgin female, head-fixed
claims.source_title: Neural circuit mechanisms of sexual receptivity in Drosophila females
claims.source_authors: Wang F, Wang K, Forknall N, Patrick C, Yang T, Parekh R, Bock D, Dickson BJ
claims.venue: Nature (seed-style attribution to Neuron is incorrect)
notes: live audit: Nature 2021 (Wang F ... Dickson BJ) confirmed; not Neuron. The result directly states that female-specific vpoDNs trigger vaginal plate opening and receive excitatory input from song-tuned vpoEN auditory neurons and from pC1. The detail about GCaMP6s soma/neurite calcium rises during song playback in virgins was not visible in the snippets, but it fits the reported song responses. bioRxiv preprint: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2020.08.07.241919v1.full

claims.claim: After mating, song responses of vpoDNs, but not of the upstream auditory vpoENs, are attenuated, which can explain why mated females are less receptive. pC1 neurons, which encode mating status and excite vpoDNs, are implicated as the source of this modulation.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster, adult female (virgin vs mated)
claims.source_title: Neural circuit mechanisms of sexual receptivity in Drosophila females
claims.source_authors: Wang F et al.
notes: live audit: The result directly states that song responses of vpoDNs, but not vpoENs, are attenuated after mating, which accounts for reduced receptivity. The paper says this modulation 'is mediated by pC1 neurons', so the claim's 'implicated' is, if anything, cautious. The result also notes that 5-second pC1 photoactivation in mated females made vpoDNs more sensitive to song and restored VPO and receptivity. The round-1 correction to MED looks overly conservative.

claims.claim: In females, optogenetic activation of Dsx+ pC1 neurons (notably pC1d/e) produces a persistent internal state lasting minutes that changes receptivity, responses to song and aggression-like behaviour. pC1 and Fru+ aIPg neurons show persistent activity after pC1 activation, and EM wiring (FAFB/FlyWire, female) shows strong recurrent pC1d/e-aIPg connections. Later work separates the contributions of pC1d and pC1e.
claims.source_title: The neural basis for a persistent internal state in Drosophila females
claims.source_authors: Deutsch D, Pacheco D, Encarnacion-Rivera L, Pereira T, Fathy R, Clemens J, Girardin C, Calhoun A, Ireland E, Burke A, Dorkenwald S, McKellar C, Macrina T, Lu R, Lee K, Kemnitz N, Ih D, Castro M, Halageri A, Jordan C, Silversmith W, Wu J, Seung HS, Murthy M (author list from memory; only 'Deutsch et al.' confirmed in results)
claims.corrected_citation: Deutsch D, Pacheco DA, Encarnacion-Rivera L, et al. (Murthy lab). The neural basis for a persistent internal state in Drosophila females. eLife 2020;9:e59502. doi:10.7554/eLife.59502. The later pC1d vs pC1e work is 'Cell type-specific contributions to a persistent aggressive internal state in female Drosophila', eLife (article 88598).
notes: live audit: Results confirm the first three authors, eLife Oct 2020, e59502, pC1d/e driving minutes-long behavioral changes in females, and recurrent pC1d/pC1e-aIPg connectivity proposed to prolong activity. The follow-up eLife paper (88598) confirms 'later work separates pC1d and pC1e'. The full 24-author list from memory was not verified beyond the first three names.

claims.claim: Baker et al. (2022) imaged and characterised 24 new auditory cell types in the fly brain (activity-recorded). Using the FlyWire female-brain connectome, they mapped connections among these types and to known early and higher-order auditory neurons (connectome-wiring). Neurons with different song-mode preferences are highly interconnected in a network without clear hierarchy, but each cell type's responses can be predicted from its inputs.
claims.source_title: Neural network organization for courtship-song feature detection in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Baker CA, McKellar C, Pang R, Nern A, Dorkenwald S, Pacheco DA, Eckstein N, Funke J, Dickson BJ, Murthy M (list from memory; Baker, Clemens?, Murthy confirmed only generally)
claims.corrected_citation: Baker CA, McKellar C, Pang R, et al. (Murthy lab). Neural network organization for courtship-song feature detection in Drosophila. Curr Biol 2022;32(15):3317-3333.e7 (published 8 Aug 2022).
notes: live audit: Results directly state: 24 new intermediate-layer auditory cell types, all synaptic connections among them mapped with FlyWire, a continuum of song-mode preferences, and neurons that are highly interconnected in a network lacking hierarchical structure. claims.claim: flymsg is an unreviewed 2026 GitHub project (releases v0.5.0/v0.5.1) that runs a whole-CNS leaky integrate-and-fire model on the MaleCNS v1.0 connectome, following Shiu et al. (Nature 2024). Its stated departures from Shiu's model are a synaptic weight rescaled for MaleCNS's denser synapse detection (w_syn 0.275/1.43 = 0.192) and no adaptive threshold (kept as an option). Its 'validation' is 29 self-defined pass/fail checks (29/29 under its own 'criterion v4') plus agreement with Shiu's brian2 model on the same connectome. The checks test whether the simulation reproduces qualitatively known circuit functions (LC4 to Giant Fiber looming escape, P1 to pIP10 song pathway, sugar to MN9, bitter leaving MN9 silent), with controls, dose-response and latency-order tests. They are not quantitative comparisons with recorded neural activity. Any new outputs it reports are untested model predictions.

claims.claim: Male D. melanogaster pattern courtship song moment to moment using feedback from the female. Whether a male sings pulse or sine song, and how bouts are structured, is largely predicted by female movement cues (her speed, and the male-female distance and position). Much song variability that looked stochastic is therefore driven by female feedback, and it depends on the male's sensory (largely visual) access to her.

Results state that much of the song pattern variability is explained by the male's dynamic sensory experience, and that males use fast changes in visual and self-motion signals to pattern song. PubMed 24598544. Refinement: the paper attributes the patterning to visual AND self-motion cues, not visual cues alone.

claims.claim: Male flies scale song amplitude with distance to the female, singing louder when farther away. This roughly compensates for the steep distance-dependent fall-off of near-field courtship sound, so the male adjusts signal intensity to the receiver's position.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster; freely courting male with virgin female

claims.claim: A GLM-HMM fit to natural male courtship identified three latent states. Each state has a different mapping from female feedback cues to song mode, and together they predict moment-to-moment song choices. Activating a pair of neurons previously considered song command neurons (pIP10, the descending song neurons) was sufficient to drive switching between states.

claims.source_title: Unsupervised identification of the internal states that shape natural behavior

notes: live audit: Nature Neuroscience 2019 (PubMed 31768056; an Author Correction also exists). The abstract as returned attributes state switching to 'a pair of neurons previously thought to be command neurons for song production'. That wording fits pIP10, a single bilateral pair of descending neurons, not the P1/pC1 cluster of about 20 cells per side. The P1/pC1 attribution in the claim is not supported by the visible text. The state labels ('close', 'chasing', 'whatever') were not visible in the results.

claims.claim: Two pulse-song types, Pfast and Pslow, were discovered in male D. melanogaster. Males choose between them according to their distance to and position relative to the female (Pslow tends to be used when close), which adds another feedback-dependent channel to the song.

notes: live audit: Current Biology 28(15):2400-2412 (2018) confirmed (PubMed 30057309; bioRxiv 221044). Results confirm the two pulse types, Pslow (lower frequency, symmetrical) and Pfast (higher frequency, asymmetrical). They also state that visual feedback influences the probability of each song mode and that four neuron types differentially affect mode choice. The specific direction (Pslow when close) was not visible in the results.

claims.claim: Male D. melanogaster sing simple single-mode trains far from the female and complex pulse-sine sequences near her. Roemschied et al. (2023) combined optogenetic manipulation (e.g., P1a, pIP10) with circuit modeling. They propose that a single brain-to-VNC pathway operates in two regimes set by recent sensory history, not parallel circuits. Brief input drives simple song. Prolonged input recruits disinhibition of VNC song circuits, which are built on mutual inhibition and rebound excitability, and so enables complex sequences near the female.

notes: live audit: Nature 2023, doi 10.1038/s41586-023-06632-1 (PubMed 37821705; PMC10600009). Results directly state: a single pathway operates in two regimes that depend on recent sensory history; males sing simple one-mode trains far from the female and complex alternating sequences near her; VNC circuits are shaped by mutual inhibition and rebound excitability. The specific optogenetic targets (P1a, pIP10) and the 622:794-801 pagination were not shown in the results.

claims.claim: Silencing individual types of lobula columnar (LC) visual projection neuron, combined with 'knockout training' of a deep network and calcium imaging, showed that the male's representation of the female that drives courtship behaviors, including song, is distributed across a population of LC types. It is not carried by a single dedicated channel.

Results directly describe knockout training, perturbation of more than a dozen visual projection neuron types, and the finding that combinations of visual projection neurons form a population code driving male interactions with the female.

claims.claim: In tethered D. melanogaster males walking on a ball, pursuit of a moving fly-sized visual target depends on P1-mediated sexual arousal. Two-photon imaging with optogenetic P1 activation showed that arousal gates how LC10a visual signals drive the pursuit. Whether the target was presented in closed or open loop, and the exact circuit site of the gating, need confirmation.

The results settle the open 'circuit site' question: the gain of LC10a visual projection neurons rises during courtship, and P1 activity continuously tunes the gain of the LC10a pathway, which in a network model almost fully specifies tracking. The closed- versus open-loop presentation detail was still not visible.

claims.claim: Thermogenetic activation of fruitless-expressing neurons elicits courtship song with no female present. The brain neurons P1 and the descending neuron pIP10 drive song in solitary males, and thoracic song neurons (e.g., dPR1, vPR6) shape song features even in decapitated flies. Song can therefore be 'written' neurally.

notes: live audit: Neuron 69(3):509-522 (2011), von Philipsborn, Liu, Yu, Masser, Bidaye, Dickson. Results state that five classes of fru neuron trigger or compose the song, and that artificial activation triggers wing extension and/or vibration in isolated males without the usual sensory inputs. The results also mention P1, vPR6 and dPR1. The decapitated-fly detail was not explicitly visible.

claims.claim: In virgin females, doublesex-expressing pC1 neurons respond to male courtship song and to the male pheromone cVA in calcium imaging. Silencing pC1 reduces receptivity, so pC1 acts as a multisensory receiver integrator.

notes: live audit: Neuron 83:149-163 (2014), Zhou, Pan, Robinett, Meissner, Baker. Results state that pC1 (and pCd) neurons respond to cVA, that pC1 also responds to male courtship song, and that silencing makes females unreceptive while activation promotes receptivity. Note that the paper implicates pCd as well as pC1.

claims.claim: The doublesex-expressing neurons pC2l and pC2m exist in both sexes and respond selectively to conspecific pulse song, with inter-pulse-interval tuning that matches behavioral preferences. Activating them drives sex-specific behavioral responses to song.

Results state that pC2 neurons are tuned to multiple temporal aspects of one song mode, that behavioral tuning is similar across sexes, and that they drive sex-specific behaviors. The pC2l/pC2m subtype names were not visible. A reissued PII (S0960-9822(23)01049-7; PubMed 37699336) also exists, apparently a 2023 re-publication or correction notice.

claims.claim: Brief optogenetic activation of female pC1 neurons produces a persistent internal state lasting minutes that changes how females respond to male song playback, and it also elicits aggressive behaviors. EM reconstruction from FAFB showed recurrent connectivity among pC1 subtypes (notably pC1d/pC1e) consistent with the persistence.

claims.claim: In D. melanogaster females, vpoDN descending neurons trigger vaginal plate opening, the acceptance behavior. vpoDN integrate excitatory input from vpoEN, which respond to conspecific pulse song, with input from pC1 neurons that reflect mating status. Activating the pathway promotes VPO (Wang et al. 2021, Nature).
