claims.corrected_citation: Wang K, Wang F, Forknall N, Yang T, Patrick C, Parekh R, Dickson BJ. Neural circuit mechanisms of sexual receptivity in Drosophila females. Nature 589(7843):577-581 (2021). doi:10.1038/s41586-020-2972-7
notes: live audit: The venue field (Neuron 109:101-118) is wrong. The paper is in Nature 589:577-581, confirmed by FlyBase FBrf0247919 and the nature.com result. Results directly confirm the content: VPO is controlled by a pair of female-specific descending neurons (vpoDNs), which receive excitatory input from song-tuned auditory vpoENs and from pC1 neurons that encode mating status.

claims.claim: Playback of artificial pulse song with the conspecific inter-pulse interval (roughly mid-30 ms) sped up mating when females were paired with wingless (mute) males, whereas songs with other intervals were less effective. This showed that a playback signal can substitute for part of the male's side of the dialogue.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster; females paired with wingless males under song playback
claims.source_title: Pulse interval as a critical parameter in the courtship song of Drosophila melanogaster
claims.source_authors: Bennet-Clark HC, Ewing AW
notes: live audit: Animal Behaviour 17:755-759 (1969), Bennet-Clark and Ewing (also ADS 1969AnBeh..17..755B). Results state a pulse interval of about 34 ms and that species specificity is set by pulse interval, not pulse length. The wingless-male playback design and the faster-mating result were not visible in the snippets.

claims.claim: The reported ~55 s oscillation in inter-pulse interval (Kyriacou-Hall song rhythm), and its claimed role in female preference, was not supported by large re-recordings and statistical reanalyses. The original authors dispute this and attribute the failures to pulse-detection problems and low-intensity courtship.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster; male song recordings (various strains)
claims.source_title: Experimental and statistical reevaluation provides no evidence for Drosophila courtship song rhythms (see also Stern 2014 BMC Biology; Kyriacou et al. 2017 PNAS rebuttal)
claims.source_authors: Stern DL, Clemens J, Coen P, Calhoun AJ, Hogenesch JB, Arthur BJ, Murthy M
notes: live audit: PNAS 114(37):9978-9983 (2017); authors match. Results state that manual, automated and new datasets give no evidence for song rhythms or for genotype differences in periodicity. Caveat: a 2021 Correction to the Supporting Information (PNAS 118(6):e2100258118) fixed a cosinor-code bug (degrees used instead of radians) that underestimated true positives. Cite it alongside the paper. The Kyriacou rebuttal was not checked.

claims.claim: D. melanogaster females produce their own wing-vibration song during copulation, and male seminal fluid modulates it. Acoustic signalling in fly courtship is therefore not one-way.
claims.source_title: Female copulation song is modulated by seminal fluid
claims.source_authors: Kerwin P, Yuan J, von Philipsborn AC
notes: live audit: Nature Communications 11:1430 (2020), Kerwin, Yuan, von Philipsborn. Results state that females sing by wing vibration during copulation, that the song requires DsxF neurons and depends on transfer of seminal fluid from the accessory gland, and that it raises male reproductive success under competition.

claims.claim: FlyMAD tracks freely walking flies and aims a laser at individual flies, even specific body regions, with low latency. It enabled thermogenetic or optogenetic activation of neurons such as P1 and pIP10 during ongoing courtship interactions.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster; freely walking and courting flies
claims.source_title: FlyMAD: rapid thermogenetic control of neuronal activity in freely walking Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Bath DE, Stowers JR, Hörmann D, Poehlmann A, Dickson BJ, Straw AD
notes: live audit: Nature Methods 2014 (doi 10.1038/nmeth.2973), Bath, Stowers, Hoermann, Poehlmann, Dickson, Straw. Results state that computer vision targets an IR laser to freely walking flies for silencing or activation within fractions of a second, demonstrated on locomotion, vision and courtship neurons. The results emphasize thermogenetic control; the optogenetic use and the specific P1/pIP10 experiments were not visible.

claims.claim: The Deep Audio Segmenter (DAS) annotates fly courtship song (pulse and sine) and bird song with deep networks, with latency low enough (milliseconds) for closed-loop experiments.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster song, plus bird and other animal vocalizations
claims.source_title: Fast and accurate annotation of acoustic signals with deep neural networks
claims.source_authors: Steinfath E, Palacios-Muñoz A, Rottschäfer JR, Yuezak D, Clemens J
notes: live audit: eLife 10:e68837 (2021), Steinfath, Palacios-Munoz, Rottschaefer, Yuezak, Clemens. Results state that DAS annotates signals from insects, birds and mammals with high throughput and low latency, allowing real-time annotation for closed-loop interventions.

claims.claim: SLEAP multi-animal pose tracking can run inference in real time, fast enough for closed-loop control. The paper demonstrated closed-loop experiments in interacting flies.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster (courting pairs) and other species
claims.source_title: SLEAP: A deep learning system for multi-animal pose tracking
claims.source_authors: Pereira TD, Tabris N, Matsliah A, Turner DM, Li J, Ravindranath S, Papadoyannis ES, Normand E, Deutsch DS, Wang ZY, et al.
notes: live audit: Nature Methods 19(4):486-495 (2022), Pereira, Tabris, Matsliah et al. (PubMed 35379947; a Publisher Correction exists). The source is confirmed, but the results did not show the real-time or closed-loop demonstration, so that part of the claim remains unverified from search text.

claims.claim: Autonomous robots coated with cockroach odor were accepted into groups of American cockroaches and shifted the mixed group's collective shelter choice, including toward a shelter the insects would not normally prefer. Robots and animals jointly determined the group decision.
claims.species: Periplaneta americana (American cockroach) groups with InsBot robots
claims.source_title: Social integration of robots into groups of cockroaches to control self-organized choices
claims.source_authors: Halloy J, Sempo G, Caprari G, Rivault C, Asadpour M, Tâche F, Saïd I, Durier V, Canonge S, Amé JM, Detrain C, Correll N, Martinoli A, Mondada F, Siegwart R, Deneubourg JL
notes: live audit: Science 318:1155-1158 (2007), Halloy, Sempo et al. (PubMed 18006751). Results state that mixed groups of cockroaches and socially integrated autonomous robots made shared shelter selections, with natural and artificial individuals perceived as equivalent. The steering toward a normally non-preferred shelter was not explicitly visible.

claims.claim: Robots placed in a honeybee arena (Graz, Austria) and a zebrafish tank (Lausanne, Switzerland) were linked, so each robot relayed its own group's behavior to the other. The two species' groups came to coordinate their collective decisions without ever meeting.
claims.species: Apis mellifera (juvenile honeybees) and Danio rerio (zebrafish), with robotic agents (ASSISIbf project)
claims.source_title: Robots mediating interactions between animals for interspecies collective behaviors
claims.source_authors: Bonnet F, Mills R, Szopek M, Schönwetter-Fuchs S, Halloy J, Bogdan S, Correia L, Mondada F, Schmickl T
notes: live audit: Science Robotics 2019, Bonnet, Mills et al. (PubMed 33137747). Results state that robots integrated into honeybee and zebrafish groups, each in a different city, enabled interspecies information transfer shown by emergent collective decisions. The city names (Graz, Lausanne) were not visible.

claims.claim: A robotic honeybee dancer (RoboBee) in an observation hive drew dance-followers, and some followers were recruited toward the advertised location, but recruitment was weaker and less consistent than for natural waggle dances.
claims.species: Apis mellifera; observation hive with a robotic dancer
claims.source_title: Dancing honey bee robot elicits dance-following and recruits foragers
claims.source_authors: Landgraf T, Bierbach D, Kirbach A, Cusing R, Oertel M, Lehmann K, Greggers U, Menzel R, Rojas R
claims.venue: arXiv preprint (1803.07126); builds on Michelsen et al. 1992 Behav Ecol Sociobiol mechanical-bee model
notes: live audit: arXiv 1803.07126 (2018), Landgraf et al., 'Dancing Honey bee Robot Elicits Dance-Following and Recruits Foragers'. Results state that RoboBee elicited natural dance-following, and that harmonic-radar tracking showed followers adjusted their flight paths using the robotic dance. The comparison claim (recruitment weaker and less consistent than natural dances) was not visible. The work is still listed as a preprint in these results.

claims.claim: Guppies were more likely to accept and follow an interactive robotic fish (RoboFish) when it had realistic eyes and moved in response to the live fish (closed-loop) rather than along fixed paths.
claims.source_title: RoboFish: increased acceptance of interactive robotic fish with realistic eyes and natural motion patterns by live Trinidadian guppies
claims.source_authors: Landgraf T, Bierbach D, Nguyen H, Muggelberg N, Romanczuk P, Krause J
notes: live audit: Bioinspiration & Biomimetics 2016 (PubMed 26757096). Results state that realistic eye dummies together with natural motion patterns significantly improved RoboFish acceptance by guppies, and they mention interactive behaviors. It was not visible that the motion contrast was specifically closed-loop responsive movement versus fixed paths. Consider wording it as 'natural (including interactive) motion patterns'.

claims.claim: Zebra finches exchanging calls with a computer-controlled 'vocal robot' learned to time their calls predictively to avoid overlapping the robot's calls. This predictive turn-taking depends on the forebrain song system.
claims.species: Taeniopygia guttata (zebra finch), females and males, interacting with a vocal robot
claims.source_title: The forebrain song system mediates predictive call timing in female and male zebra finches
claims.source_authors: Benichov JI, Benezra SE, Vallentin D, Globerson E, Long MA, Tchernichovski O
notes: live audit: Current Biology (Feb 2016), Benichov, Benezra, Vallentin, Globerson, Long, Tchernichovski (PubMed 26774786). Results state that birds exchanging calls with a vocal robot adjusted call timing to avoid jamming by predicting the robot's pattern. Lesioning the song-system nucleus RA impaired the timing adjustment, while birds still responded to the robot. Females showed better timing plasticity.

claims.claim: In zebra finches, inhibition within the premotor nucleus HVC controls when a bird calls back to a partner in turn-taking. Recordings and manipulation of HVC activity linked inhibitory interneuron activity to the timing of vocal replies.
claims.species: Taeniopygia guttata (zebra finch); HVC recordings and manipulation during call exchanges
claims.source_title: Inhibition within a premotor circuit controls the timing of vocal turn-taking in zebra finches
claims.source_authors: Benichov JI, Vallentin D
notes: live audit: Nature Communications 2020 (doi 10.1038/s41467-019-13938-0), Benichov and Vallentin. Results state that local inhibition in a cortical premotor nucleus (HVC) precedes call-related premotor activity, and that pharmacologically blocking inhibition speeds responses and impairs flexible overlap avoidance. The manipulation was pharmacological.

claims.claim: Neural recordings from both members of plain-tailed wren pairs singing duets in their natural habitat (Ecuadorian Andes) showed that auditory input from the partner modulates activity in each bird's premotor HVC. This coordinates the rapid alternation of syllables between partners.
claims.species: Pheugopedius euophrys (plain-tailed wren), male-female duetting pairs, field neurophysiology
claims.source_title: Neurophysiological coordination of duet singing (see also Fortune et al. 2011 Science 334:666-670)
claims.source_authors: Coleman MJ, Day NF, Rivera-Parra P, Fortune ES
notes: live audit: PNAS 118(23) (2021), Coleman, Day, Rivera-Parra, Fortune; field recordings in Ecuador. Refinement: the partner's auditory cues produced INHIBITION (decreases) of HVC activity that alternated with each bird's own premotor activity, a more specific statement than 'modulates'.

claims.claim: Playback of a recorded humpback 'whup/throp' contact call to a free-ranging female humpback whale ('Twain') in Southeast Alaska produced an extended exchange. The whale approached and gave about three dozen call responses over roughly 20 minutes, with timing that tracked the playback intervals.
claims.species: Megaptera novaeangliae (humpback whale), one adult female, field interactive playback
claims.source_title: Interactive bioacoustic playback as a tool for detecting and exploring nonhuman intelligence: 'conversing' with an Alaskan humpback whale
claims.source_authors: McCowan B, Hubbard J, Walker L, Fournet M, Doyle L, et al.
notes: live audit: PeerJ 2023, article 16349 (PMC10693240; bioRxiv 2023.02.05.527130). Results state a 20-minute exchange in which a recorded 'whup/throp' contact call was broadcast to adult female 'Twain' in Southeast Alaska. The results also describe latency and temporal-matching analyses across three phases (engagement, agitation, disengagement). The '~three dozen responses' count was not visible. The 'intentional' framing is the authors' interpretation.

claims.claim: CHAT (Cetacean Hearing Augmentation Telemetry) is an underwater wearable computer. Researchers use it with free-ranging Atlantic spotted dolphins to play synthetic whistles associated with objects and to detect in real time whether dolphins mimic those whistles, as a platform for two-way communication experiments.
claims.species: Stenella frontalis (Atlantic spotted dolphin), wild, Bahamas (Wild Dolphin Project) with human divers
claims.source_title: An underwater wearable computer for two way human-dolphin communication experimentation
claims.source_authors: Kohlsdorf D, Gilliland S, Presti P, Starner T, Herzing D
claims.venue: ISWC 2013 (Proceedings of the International Symposium on Wearable Computers)
notes: live audit: The CHAT system is confirmed via the Georgia Tech GVU Center project page and the 2025 Google DolphinGemma blog. The blog describes CHAT as associating novel synthetic whistles with objects (scarves, seaweed) in the hope that dolphins mimic them to request the items. The cited ISWC 2013 paper (Kohlsdorf et al.) was NOT surfaced by any search, so the citation itself remains unverified.

claims.claim: Google, Georgia Tech and the Wild Dolphin Project announced DolphinGemma, a roughly 400M-parameter audio model trained on the Wild Dolphin Project's Atlantic spotted dolphin recordings. It uses SoundStream tokenization to predict likely next vocalization sounds and is intended to run on smartphones within the CHAT field system. The announcement contained no peer-reviewed evaluation of meaning.
claims.source_title: DolphinGemma announcement (Google blog / press, April 2025)
claims.source_authors: Google DeepMind/Google with Georgia Tech (Starner) and Wild Dolphin Project (Herzing)
notes: live audit: Google blog (April 2025) with Georgia Tech and the Wild Dolphin Project. Results state that the model uses the SoundStream tokenizer, has about 400M parameters, runs on Pixel phones in the field, is trained on Atlantic spotted dolphin vocalizations, and generates novel dolphin-like sound sequences. It is presented as a corporate announcement; no peer-reviewed evaluation appeared in the results.

claims.claim: In a rat 'brain-to-brain interface', cortical activity recorded from an encoder rat performing a tactile or visual discrimination was delivered as intracortical microstimulation to a decoder rat. The decoder chose correctly above chance, with modest accuracy of roughly 60-70% against 50% chance, and the encoder was rewarded when the decoder was correct, closing a dyadic loop.
neurons: M1/S1 cortex ensembles (encoder); ICMS target cortex (decoder)
claims.source_title: A brain-to-brain interface for real-time sharing of sensorimotor information
claims.source_authors: Pais-Vieira M, Lebedev M, Kunicki C, Wang J, Nicolelis MAL
notes: live audit: Scientific Reports 3:1319 (28 Feb 2013), Pais-Vieira, Lebedev, Kunicki, Wang, Nicolelis. Results confirm the encoder rat performing tactile or visual two-choice tasks, transmission via ICMS to a decoder rat, and an Internet link from Natal to Durham. The specific accuracy figures (~60-70%) and the encoder-reward loop were not visible.

claims.claim: A non-invasive brain-to-brain interface linked a human's EEG (steady-state visual evoked potentials expressing intent) to transcranial focused ultrasound over an anesthetized rat's motor cortex. It triggered rat tail movements with high reported accuracy (about 94%).
claims.species: Human operators and anesthetized Sprague-Dawley rats
claims.source_title: Non-invasive brain-to-brain interface (BBI): establishing functional links between two brains
claims.source_authors: Yoo SS, Kim H, Filandrianos E, Taghados SJ, Park S
notes: live audit: PLoS ONE 2013, Yoo, Kim, Filandrianos, Taghados, Park. Results state that an SSVEP-based BMI extracted human intention and drove transcranial focused ultrasound to an anesthetized rat's brain, moving its tail with 94.0 +/- 3.0% accuracy and a 1.59 +/- 1.07 s delay.

claims.claim: Male Adult Nerve Cord (MANC) connectome analysis identified nested premotor circuits in the ventral nerve cord that generate pulse versus sine song. Some neurons are shared and some are specific to one song type, and optogenetic tests supported their roles.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster; male VNC connectome (MANC) plus behavioral activation
claims.source_title: Nested neural circuits generate distinct acoustic signals during Drosophila courtship
claims.source_authors: Lillvis JL, Wang K, Shiozaki HM, Xu M, Stern DL, Dickson BJ
notes: live audit: Current Biology 2024 (PII S0960-9822(24)00015-0; bioRxiv 2023.08.30.555537). Results state that MANC analysis expanded the male song circuits into a highly interconnected core of eight fru and/or dsx cell types organized as two nested feedforward pathways: the smaller generates sine song and the larger generates pulse song. Author list and 34:808-824 pagination were not shown in the snippets. A related follow-up, 'Activity of nested neural circuits drives different courtship songs in Drosophila' (PMC11452343), also appeared.

claims.claim: Baker et al. (2022) combined FlyWire EM reconstruction with calcium imaging during song playback. Auditory neurons in the Drosophila central brain show a continuum of pulse and sine song preferences. Cell types with different preferences are highly interconnected in a non-hierarchical network. Each cell type's song responses can nonetheless be predicted from its synaptic inputs.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster; females; EM reconstruction plus two-photon imaging with song playback
claims.source_title: Neural network organization for courtship-song feature detection in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Baker CA, McKellar C, Pang R, Nern A, Dorkenwald S, Pacheco DA, Eckstein N, Funke J, Dickson BJ, Murthy M
notes: live audit: Current Biology 32(15):3317-3333.e7 (2022), Baker, McKellar, Pang, Nern, Dorkenwald, Pacheco et al. (PubMed 35793679). Results directly state that 24 new auditory cell types were mapped with FlyWire, that neurons show a continuum of song-mode preferences, and that they are highly interconnected in a network lacking hierarchy. The final clause (responses predictable from synaptic inputs) was not visible; drop it or verify it separately. Note: my own 30-search budget was fully used; the shared session cap was never hit.

new_leads_unverified.claim: Using real-time closed-loop optogenetics, activating female 'moonwalker' descending neurons each time the male sang pulse song made females walk backward. Males exposed to this aberrant female feedback changed their mapping from social context to song choice, kept the altered strategies with normal females, and produced a novel song strategy. This shows learning from recent social experience in innate courtship song.
new_leads_unverified.source_title: Recent social experience alters song behavior in Drosophila
new_leads_unverified.why_it_matters: This is the closest existing experiment to a closed-loop 'artificial partner' in the fly. The experimenter rewrites the receiver's feedback in real time and the sender adapts, which directly supports the track's two-way communication thesis. A Nature Reviews Neuroscience highlight (s41583-026-01043-3) covered it.

new_leads_unverified.claim: A complete male Drosophila central nervous system connectome (brain plus nerve cord) was analyzed for sexual dimorphism, following the 2025 completion of CNS connectomes (Bates et al.; Berg et al.).
new_leads_unverified.source_title: Sexual dimorphism in the complete Drosophila male central nervous system connectome
new_leads_unverified.why_it_matters: It provides a single wiring diagram linking the male brain's sensory and decision neurons (P1, LC10a, auditory pathway) to the VNC song circuits, which the claim list currently cites only from separate FAFB and MANC datasets.

new_leads_unverified.claim: A new 2026 Current Biology study addresses how distinct wing behaviors are sequenced during Drosophila courtship; its specific findings were not visible in the search snippets.
new_leads_unverified.source_title: Sequencing of distinct wing behaviors during Drosophila courtship
new_leads_unverified.why_it_matters: It likely extends Roemschied 2023 on song sequencing and could update claims T06-05 and T06-31 on how the song motor program is ordered.

new_leads_unverified.claim: Sexually dimorphic and sex-specific VNC intrinsic neurons are strongly interconnected and concentrated in the wing tectulum and abdominal neuromere. Females, although they do not sing, retain several sexually dimorphic song neurons.
new_leads_unverified.source_title: Uncovering Sex Differences in the Drosophila Ventral Nerve Cord Through Connectome Alignment
new_leads_unverified.why_it_matters: It compares male (MANC) and female (FANC) nerve cords, which bears on the receiver side and on how song circuits map across sexes.

new_leads_unverified.claim: A 2025 review synthesizes how the neural circuits for Drosophila courtship song evolve, across species and circuit levels.
new_leads_unverified.source_title: Neural evolution of complex motor behaviors: insights from Drosophila courtship song
new_leads_unverified.why_it_matters: It is an up-to-date synthesis for the song-production side of the track and a good check that the claim list reflects current consensus.

new_leads_unverified.claim: A 2025 report surveys the state of connectome-based brain emulation, including Drosophila whole-brain connectome models.
new_leads_unverified.source_title: State of Brain Emulation Report 2025
new_leads_unverified.why_it_matters: It bears on whether connectome-constrained fly models are mature enough to act as an in-silico 'partner' in closed-loop communication experiments, the track's anchor premise. It is a secondary source, so read critically.

claims.claim: NatureLM-audio (Earth Species Project) is an audio-language foundation model for bioacoustics. It combines a BEATs audio encoder with a Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct backbone, answers natural-language questions about animal audio zero-shot, and reported state-of-the-art zero-shot classification of unseen species. Weights, code and benchmark data were released.
claims.species: Multi-taxa (birds, mammals, others); trained on bioacoustics plus speech and music text-audio pairs
claims.source_title: NatureLM-audio: an Audio-Language Foundation Model for Bioacoustics
claims.source_authors: Robinson D, Miron M, Hagiwara M, Pietquin O
notes: live audit: Results (arXiv, ICLR 2025 poster page, OpenReview PDF headed 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025', HF model card, GitHub) confirm the authors Robinson, Miron, Hagiwara and Pietquin. They also confirm the BEATs encoder with Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, training on bioacoustics, speech and music text-audio pairs, state-of-the-art zero-shot classification of unseen species, and open release of weights, benchmark data and code.

claims.claim: BEANS-Zero is ESP's test-only zero-shot benchmark for audio-language models. It adds call-type prediction, life-stage classification, captioning and individual counting on top of species classification and detection.
claims.source_title: EarthSpeciesProject/BEANS-Zero (Hugging Face dataset)
claims.source_authors: Earth Species Project
claims.venue: Hugging Face; introduced in the NatureLM-audio paper
claims.corrected_citation: Introduced in Robinson D et al., NatureLM-audio, arXiv 2411.07186 (2024) / ICLR 2025; dataset hosted at Hugging Face EarthSpeciesProject/BEANS-Zero.
notes: live audit: The NatureLM-audio results say the model was evaluated on a 'novel benchmark called BEANS-Zero' and list tasks including species classification, detection, captioning and lifestage classification. Call-type prediction, individual counting and the 'test-only' description were not visible in the results. The HF dataset URL did not appear in the results, so the introducing paper is given instead. The benchmark was first described in the Nov 2024 arXiv paper, so year 2024/2025 (ICLR 2025) fits better than 2025 alone.

claims.claim: Sperm whale codas have combinatorial structure: rhythm and tempo can each be discretised, and 'rubato' (fine inter-click-interval changes relative to preceding codas) and 'ornamentation' (extra clicks) vary with conversational context. The repertoire is nearly an order of magnitude larger in distinguishable codas than previously described. The authors call this a 'sperm whale phonetic alphabet'.
claims.species: Sperm whale (Physeter macrocephalus), Eastern Caribbean (Dominica) social units
claims.source_title: Contextual and combinatorial structure in sperm whale vocalisations
claims.source_authors: Sharma P, Gero S, Payne R, Gruber DF, Rus D, Torralba A, Andreas J (Project CETI / MIT CSAIL)
claims.corrected_citation: Sharma P et al. (2024) Contextual and combinatorial structure in sperm whale vocalisations. Nature Communications 15:3617.
notes: live audit: The title, venue (Nature Communications, 2024) and authors (Sharma, Gero, Payne et al.) all match. The result text directly says codas have contextual and combinatorial structure, that 'rubato' and 'ornamentation' are sensitive to conversational context, and that they combine with the context-independent features rhythm and tempo to give a large inventory of distinguishable codas. The snippets did not show the phrase 'sperm whale phonetic alphabet' or the 'nearly an order of magnitude larger' figure. Both match my memory of the paper's main text but were not seen live.

claims.claim: Sperm whale codas have discrete spectral categories: one-formant 'a-coda vowels' and two-formant 'i-coda vowels'. These are orthogonal to rhythm-based coda types, recur across individuals, are used in dialogues, and are argued to be actively controlled rather than artefacts of movement.
claims.source_title: Vowel- and Diphthong-Like Spectral Patterns in Sperm Whale Codas
claims.source_authors: Beguš G et al. (UC Berkeley / Project CETI)
notes: live audit: Results confirm the paper in Open Mind (2025), authors Begus G, Sprouse RL, Leban A, Silva M, Gero S (PubMed 41210602). Result text supports: two recurrent discrete coda-level spectral patterns ('a- and i-coda vowels'), used in dialogues, not a physical artefact of whale movement, combining freely with traditionally analysed (rhythm) properties, plus diphthong-like patterns. The one-formant versus two-formant detail and recurrence across individuals were not visible. Suggested citation: Begus G, Sprouse RL, Leban A, Silva M, Gero S (2025) Open Mind, doi:10.1162/OPMI.a.252.

claims.claim: DolphinGemma (Google with the Wild Dolphin Project and Georgia Tech, April 2025) is a ~400M-parameter audio-in/audio-out model. It uses the SoundStream tokenizer, was trained on WDP recordings of Atlantic spotted dolphins collected since 1985, and predicts likely next sounds in a sequence. It is sized to run on Pixel phones in the field.
claims.source_title: DolphinGemma: How Google AI is helping decode dolphin communication
claims.source_authors: Google (with Wild Dolphin Project and Georgia Tech)
claims.corrected_citation: Google (Herzing D / WDP; Starner T / Georgia Tech), 'DolphinGemma: How Google AI is helping decode dolphin communication', Google Keyword blog, 14 April 2025.
notes: live audit: The Google blog (April 2025) and several news write-ups confirm the claim: a collaboration of Google, Georgia Tech and the Wild Dolphin Project; the SoundStream tokenizer; about 400M parameters, sized to run on Pixel phones in the field; prediction of the next vocalization; and training on WDP data from Atlantic spotted dolphins in the Bahamas studied since 1985.

claims.claim: The WDP/Georgia Tech CHAT system (Cetacean Hearing Augmentation Telemetry) tries two-way interaction by pairing synthetic whistles with objects dolphins like, hoping dolphins will mimic them to request the objects. DolphinGemma is meant to speed recognition of those whistles.
claims.source_title: Google Introduces DolphinGemma to Support Dolphin Communication Research
claims.source_authors: InfoQ (reporting on Google/WDP/Georgia Tech)
claims.corrected_citation: Primary: Google Keyword blog, 'DolphinGemma: How Google AI is helping decode dolphin communication' (April 2025). Secondary: InfoQ (2025).
notes: live audit: The result text directly describes CHAT (Cetacean Hearing Augmentation Telemetry) as a WDP/Georgia Tech two-way system. It assigns synthetic whistles to objects dolphins like (seagrass, scarves) and waits to see if dolphins mimic them to request the objects. The specific point that DolphinGemma is meant to speed recognition of mimicked whistles was not visible in the snippets. The InfoQ secondary source also appeared at https://www.infoq.com/news/2025/05/dolphin-gemma-google, but the primary Google blog is the better citation.

claims.claim: Signature whistles make up roughly half of wild Sarasota Bay bottlenose dolphin whistles. Among the remaining non-signature whistles, Sayigh et al. (2025 preprint) found stereotyped types shared across many individuals. In playbacks one type (NSW-A) elicited avoidance, suggesting an alarm function, and another (NSW-B) occurred in response to unexpected situations, suggesting a 'query' function. Both functions are preliminary.
claims.species: Common bottlenose dolphin (Tursiops truncatus), Sarasota Bay, Florida
claims.source_title: First evidence for widespread sharing of stereotyped non-signature whistle types by wild dolphins
claims.source_authors: Sayigh LS et al. (WHOI; Sarasota Dolphin Research Program)
notes: live audit: Results confirm the bioRxiv preprint (2025) by Sayigh et al. Non-signature whistles make up about 50% of Sarasota dolphin whistles. 22 shared NSW types were found; NSWA was produced by at least 25 dolphins and NSWB by at least 35. In playbacks NSWA drew mostly negative responses (suggesting an alarm function), and NSWB drew varying responses, consistent with a suggested 'query' function when something unexpected or unfamiliar is heard. The claim's wording is accurate and appropriately hedged. Optional additions: '22 shared types' and the individual counts.

claims.claim: The 2026 Coller-Dolittle US$100,000 prize (Jeremy Coller Foundation and Tel Aviv University, announced 26 June 2026) went to Julie E. Elie (Theunissen Lab, UC Berkeley) for showing that zebra finches classify their calls by meaning more than by acoustics. Irene Pepperberg received a Lifetime Achievement Award for her grey parrot work.
claims.species: Zebra finch (Taeniopygia guttata); grey parrot (Psittacus erithacus) for the lifetime award

claims.claim: Zebra finches trained in an operant button-press task to discriminate 11 call types made errors that tracked shared meaning rather than acoustic similarity. They confused acoustically very different long- and short-distance contact calls, but never confused a short contact call with an acoustically similar short alarm call.

claims.source_authors: Elie JE, Theunissen FE et al.
notes: live audit: Results confirm Science, 18 Sept 2025 (PubMed 40966354; bioRxiv 2024.11.14.623689). Authors: Elie JE, de Witasse-Thezy A, Thomas L, Malit B, Theunissen FE. Birds discriminated and categorised all ~11 call types, and systematic errors were more frequent between call types used in similar behavioural contexts than acoustic similarity predicted. The specific examples (long- vs short-distance contact calls confused; short contact call never confused with the acoustically similar alarm call) were not visible in the results. Keep them only if checked against the paper, or soften 'never'.

claims.claim: The 2025 Coller-Dolittle finalists were Sayigh (WHOI, dolphins; the eventual winner), Vallentin and Clemens (nightingales, with an AI model that generates and analyses whistles for interactive exchanges), Cohen-Bodénès and Neri (cuttlefish arm-wave signs), and Omer and Oren (Hebrew University, marmosets).

(dolphins, winner), Vallentin and Clemens (nightingales), Cohen-Bodenes and Neri (cuttlefish), Omer and Oren (marmosets). The WHOI-led team, with Brookfield Zoo Chicago's Sarasota Dolphin Research Program, won. The nightingale 'AI model that generates and analyses whistles' detail was not visible in the results.

claims.claim: Marmosets use phee calls to label specific conspecifics. Machine-learning classifiers found receiver-specific call features in natural phee-call dialogues, and in real-time computer-playback experiments marmosets responded more accurately when a call was directed at them.

claims.source_authors: Oren G, ..., Omer DY

Indirect support only: the Jaakkola commentary summary describes the Oren et al. study as showing receiver-specific information in marmoset phee calls, with receivers responding more to calls directed at them. A 2025 reply titled 'Vocal labeling of others by nonhuman primates: A response to Jaakkola (2025)' (PubMed 40866605) confirms the original title. The Science URL, the ML-classifier detail and the real-time playback detail were not directly seen.

claims.claim: Wild African savanna elephants address one another with individually specific rumbles. Machine learning predicted the receiver from a call's acoustic structure (469 rumbles, Amboseli and Samburu/Buffalo Springs, 1986-2022), apparently without imitation of the receiver's own calls. In playbacks, elephants responded more strongly (calling back or approaching) to calls originally addressed to them.

claims.source_title: African elephants address one another with individually specific name-like calls
claims.source_authors: Pardo MA, Fristrup K, Lolchuragi DS, Poole JH, Granli P, Moss C, Douglas-Hamilton I, Wittemyer G
notes: live audit: Confirmed as Pardo et al., Nature Ecology & Evolution 8:1353-1364 (2024). The result text directly states: 469 calls from wild female/calf groups in Amboseli and Samburu/Buffalo Springs, 1986-2022; machine learning predicted the receiver above chance (about 27.5% accuracy); playback experiments were run. The snippets did not show the specific playback response details (calling back or approaching), but they are consistent with the paper.

claims.claim: Berthet et al. reported that every bonobo call type occurs in at least one compositional combination, and that three combinations show 'nontrivial' compositionality, where one call modifies the meaning of the other. They inferred meaning from contextual features using a multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) pipeline.
claims.source_title: Extensive compositionality in the vocal system of bonobos
claims.source_authors: Berthet M, Surbeck M, Townsend SW et al.
claims.corrected_citation: Berthet M, Surbeck M, Townsend SW (2025) Extensive compositionality in the vocal system of bonobos. Science 388(6742/6743):104-108. doi:10.1126/science.adv1170
notes: live audit: Results (Science page, ADS 2025Sci...388..104B) confirm Berthet, Surbeck and Townsend (2025), Science 388:104. Using distributional-semantics methods, 'each call type ... occur[s] in at least one compositional combination' and three combinations show nontrivial compositionality; the pipeline was MCA-based. Caveat: a 2026 PeerJ reanalysis (T07-15) reports no statistically significant evidence, so this claim should be paired with it.

claims.claim: A reanalysis found that the Berthet et al. (2025) MCA pipeline flagged significant call-context relationships in 34.5-84.3% of randomised datasets with no true association. A full permutation test that respects the data's dependence structure gave a non-significant result on the original data (Monte Carlo p = 0.2597).
claims.source_title: Structure without semantics: no evidence for bonobo compositionality in Berthet et al. (2025)
claims.source_authors: Authors not captured in search results
notes: live audit: Results (PeerJ, PubMed 42644090, PMC13505523) confirm the 2026 PeerJ article 'Structure without semantics: no evidence for bonobo compositionality in Berthet et al. (2025)'. The MCA pipeline found significant relationships in 34.5-84.3% of randomised simulations, and a full permutation test on the original data gave Monte Carlo p = 0.2597. The authors argue that dependence-aware inference and theoretically motivated feature selection are both missing from the original analysis. Author names were still not visible (a Warwick WRAP repository entry appeared alongside, possibly a Warwick author, not confirmed). Round-1 'unverified/LOW' should be raised.

claims.claim: Wild Tai chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes verus) produce at least 16 different two-call combinations, drawn from a corpus of more than 12,000 recorded calls. From associations with the observed context, the authors describe four ways a call's meaning changes in combination: adding meaning, narrowing/clarifying meaning, non-compositional creation of a new meaning, and order effects. The meanings are inferred from context without playback tests, so the semantic interpretations remain hypotheses.
claims.species: Western chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes verus), Taï National Park, Côte d'Ivoire
claims.source_title: Versatile use of chimpanzee call combinations promotes meaning expansion
claims.source_authors: Girard-Buttoz C, ..., Crockford C
claims.corrected_citation: Girard-Buttoz C et al. (2025) Versatile use of chimpanzee call combinations promotes meaning expansion. Science Advances 11(19), published 9 May 2025. doi:10.1126/sciadv.adq2879
notes: live audit: Only the placeholder needed fixing. Results (Science Advances page, MPG, phys.org, ScienceDaily) state '>12,000 calls', 'at least 16 different two-call combinations' and four meaning-change mechanisms. The substance of the claim is correct.

claims.claim: In Egyptian fruit BATS (not fruit flies) monitored around the clock with audio and video for months, machine learning on ~15,000 everyday social vocalizations recovered the emitter's identity, the behavioural context, the listener's response and, partly, the call's addressee.
claims.species: Egyptian fruit bat (Rousettus aegyptiacus), captive colony
claims.source_title: Everyday bat vocalizations contain information about emitter, addressee, context, and behavior
claims.source_authors: Prat Y, Taub M, Yovel Y
notes: live audit: Confirmed as Prat, Taub & Yovel, Scientific Reports 6:39419 (22 Dec 2016). The result text directly states that about 15,000 vocalizations from 22 Egyptian fruit bats were recorded over 75 days and that they carry information on emitter identity, context, behavioural response and even addressee. 'Months' is accurate, since the recording ran about 2.5 months.

claims.claim: Wireless neural recordings in the frontal cortex of groups of freely communicating Egyptian fruit bats showed that neural activity represented the identity of the vocalizing group member. Vocalizations by bats in the same cluster produced more accurate identity coding and higher brain-to-brain synchrony across the group.
claims.species: Egyptian fruit bat (Rousettus aegyptiacus), captive groups
claims.source_title: Cortical representation of group social communication in bats
claims.source_authors: Rose MC, Styr B, Schmid TA, Elie JE, Yartsev MM

The result text directly confirms that vocalizations elicited brain-to-brain synchrony (high-frequency LFP) between group members, and that this synchrony was abolished outside the group social context. The snippets did not show the frontal-cortex identity coding or the finding that same-cluster calls gave better identity coding and synchrony. The summary also did not list first author Rose MC. Prefer the /doi/ URL over the /doi/abs/ URL.

claims.claim: Hippocampal CA1 neurons in freely behaving wild Egyptian fruit bats living as a group in a lab cave encode the identity and sex of other bats. The strength of identity coding depends on the other bat's sex, hierarchy rank and social affiliation.
claims.species: Egyptian fruit bat (Rousettus aegyptiacus), mixed-sex groups of 5-10 wild-caught bats

notes: live audit: Results confirm the title, authors, Science 387(6733), 31 Jan 2025, and the setup: CA1 neurons, a mixed-sex group of 5-10 freely behaving wild Egyptian fruit bats in a lab cave, place cells that were socially modulated and represented conspecific identity and sex. Hierarchy and affiliation modulation is in the title; the specific dependence was not detailed in the snippet.

claims.claim: Realistic zebra finch song (pitch, amplitude and timbre) can be synthesised directly from neural activity recorded in a premotor song nucleus. One method maps activity into a low-dimensional biomechanical model of the vocal organ, the syrinx.
claims.source_title: Neurally driven synthesis of learned, complex vocalizations
claims.source_authors: Arneodo EM, Chen S, Brown DE, Gilja V, Gentner TQ
claims.corrected_citation: Arneodo EM, Chen S, Brown DE, Gilja V, Gentner TQ (2021) Neurally driven synthesis of learned, complex vocalizations. Current Biology 31(15):3419-3425.e5. doi:10.1016/j.cub.2021.05.035
notes: live audit: The result text directly states that zebra finch song was reproduced from premotor neural activity down to pitch, volume and timbre, using a low-dimensional biomechanical model of the vocal organ. The page range is 3419-3425.e5.

claims.claim: DAS (Deep Audio Segmenter) uses a temporal-convolutional network to annotate acoustic signals sample by sample from raw audio. It was validated on Drosophila courtship song (pulse and sine), mouse ultrasonic vocalizations and Bengalese finch song.
claims.species: Drosophila melanogaster (male courtship song); Mus musculus; Lonchura striata domestica
claims.source_title: Fast and accurate annotation of acoustic signals with deep neural networks
claims.source_authors: Steinfath E, Palacios-Muñoz A, Rottschäfer JR, Yuezak D, Clemens J

The result text directly states that DAS uses temporal convolutional networks with dilated convolutions and was evaluated on fly courtship song, mouse USVs and Bengalese finch song. From memory, the paper also covers other species (e.g. zebra finch, marmoset), so the three species in the claim are a subset. That is not an error.

claims.claim: SongExplorer is a browser-based deep-learning workflow for discovering, annotating and segmenting animal acoustic signals, including substrate vibrations. It is more accurate than heuristic segmenters, about as accurate as two expert human annotators, and allows rapid detection of song types in new species and of new song types in well-studied ones.

Cite bioRxiv as the primary source rather than the Janelia page. The point about detecting song types in new species was not visible in the snippets.

The spectrogram-as-image framing is implied by the object-detector architecture.

claims.claim: A GLM-HMM fit without supervision to male-female courtship tracking data found three latent internal states in male D. melanogaster. Each state maps sensory feedback cues (mainly from the female) to song choices (pulse, sine, no song) differently, and together they predict moment-to-moment song patterning. These are model states inferred from behaviour, not recorded neural activity. Optogenetic activation of pIP10, a pair of descending neurons previously considered song command neurons, was sufficient to shift the male between states (causal manipulation).
neurons: song-pathway 'command-like' neuron pair (identity to confirm in full text; candidates pIP10 or P1/pC1)

claims.source_authors: Calhoun AJ, Pillow JW, Murthy M

notes: live audit: Results confirm Calhoun, Pillow and Murthy, Nature Neuroscience 22(12):2040-2049 (Dec 2019; PubMed 31768056). An unsupervised model uncovered three latent states in courting males, which predicted moment-to-moment song-patterning decisions; the states are different sensorimotor strategies mapping feedback cues to song modes. The pIP10 optogenetic state-switching result was not visible in the search results, so it is unconfirmed live. There is also an Author Correction (s41593-019-0571-4) that may be worth citing.

claims.claim: Whole-central-brain volumetric calcium imaging with cross-brain registration showed that auditory (song-like) stimuli evoke responses in 33 of 36 major central-brain regions of D. melanogaster, in both sexes. Most responses were tuned to courtship-song features, including in regions tied to other senses and to motor control.

The result text states the use of volumetric imaging with across-brain registration, and that auditory activity is present in most central brain regions and in neurons responsive to other modalities. The snippets did not show the exact '33 of 36 regions' figure, the both-sexes detail or the tuning to courtship-song features.

claims.claim: Imaged D. melanogaster auditory neurons show a continuum of preferences across courtship-song modes (pulse vs sine) and response timescales. Neurons with different preferences are highly interconnected in a network that lacks hierarchical structure, as shown by combining activity imaging with connectome anatomy.
neurons: central-brain auditory neurons with pulse/sine preferences (e.g., pathways including pC1)

The results show the study of feature selectivity for sine versus pulse song, plus 24 new intermediate-layer auditory cell types identified with a connectomic resource. The snippets did not show the specific 'continuum of preferences' and 'lacks hierarchical structure' findings.

claims.claim: In male D. melanogaster, calcium imaging shows that vPN1 neurons respond preferentially to pulse song with short IPIs, and pC1 responses across IPIs closely match males' behavioural chaining response. Optogenetic activation of vPN1 or pC1 in solitary males elicits courtship behaviours.

The result text confirms the male-specific aPN1-vPN1-pC1 song pathway and that inactivating vPN1 or pC1 disrupts song-induced chaining. The snippets did not show the calcium-imaging IPI tuning or the optogenetic activation details, though they are consistent with the abstract as I remember it. Prefer the eLife URL over the PMC link.

claims.source_authors: Rutz C, Bronstein M, Raskin A, et al.

claims.claim: In male mice, intersectionally labeled periaqueductal gray neurons that were transiently active during courtship USVs (PAG-USV neurons) are necessary for USVs: silencing them abolished USVs and impaired attraction of females. Activating them triggered USVs even without female cues.

claims.source_authors: Tschida K, Michael V, Takatoh J, Han BX, Zhao S, Sakurai K, Mooney R, Wang F

notes: live audit: Tschida et al., Neuron 2019 confirmed (PMID 31204083). The search summary says directly that intersectional labeling of PAG neurons transiently active during male courtship USVs was used, that genetic silencing left males unable to produce USVs and impaired their ability to attract females, and that activation triggered USVs even without female cues. The claim matches.

Volume and pages 34(5):1107-1113.e3 were not visible in the results.

claims.source_authors: Ziobro P, Zheng D-J, et al., Tschida K (corresponding)

It was published in eNeuro on 17 Aug 2026, co-first authors Ziobro P and Zheng D-J, corresponding author Tschida K; there is also a bioRxiv preprint (10.64898/2026.03.18.712517). claims.claim: Excitatory, vocalization-specific laryngeal premotor neurons in the retroambiguus nucleus (RAmVOC) are necessary and sufficient for vocal-cord closure and USV production. claims.claim: In male Alston's singing mice, orofacial motor cortex (OMC) is needed for the rapid, flexible vocal responses that support countersinging. Note structure largely survives OMC inactivation, which implies the notes are generated by downstream circuits (presumed subcortical, not identified in the study), with OMC modulating them.

claims.corrected_citation: Okobi DE Jr, Banerjee A, Matheson AMM, Phelps SM, Long MA. Motor cortical control of vocal interaction in neotropical singing mice. Science 2019;363(6430):983-988.

The results describe an orofacial motor cortical region, hierarchical control of vocal production, and motor cortex setting the pace of singing moment by moment in S. teguina countersinging. That fits the claim. The specific point that note structure survives OMC inactivation does not appear in the result text. The claim's wording that the downstream generator is presumed subcortical and was not identified in the study is appropriately hedged.

claims.claim: In socially interacting zebra finches, local inhibition in the premotor nucleus HVC precedes premotor activity linked to calling. Blocking inhibition in HVC makes call replies faster and impairs the birds' ability to avoid overlapping their partner.
claims.source_title: Inhibition within a premotor circuit controls the timing of vocal turn-taking in zebra finches
claims.source_authors: Benichov JI, Vallentin D
claims.corrected_citation: Benichov JI, Vallentin D. Inhibition within a premotor circuit controls the timing of vocal turn-taking in zebra finches. Nature Communications 11:221 (2020).
notes: live audit: Benichov and Vallentin, Nat Commun 11:221 (2020) confirmed. The abstract text in the results says directly that local inhibition precedes premotor activation linked to calling, and that blocking inhibition gives faster vocal responses and impairs the birds' ability to flexibly avoid overlapping a partner.

claims.claim: In zebra finches, HVC neurons that project to RA (HVC(RA)) each fire one short burst of a few spikes (usually cited as about 6 ms) at a single precise time in the song motif. The bursts are repeatable across renditions and occur in sequence across the population. The authors propose that this ultra-sparse sequence acts as an explicit clock for song timing (activity-recorded; the timing role is the authors' interpretation).
claims.source_title: An ultra-sparse code underlies the generation of neural sequences in a songbird
claims.source_authors: Hahnloser RHR, Kozhevnikov AA, Fee MS
notes: live audit: Hahnloser, Kozhevnikov and Fee, Nature 419:65-70 (2002) confirmed. The results state that HVC(RA) neurons burst sparsely at a single precise time, fire in sequence relative to one another, and as a population form 'an explicit representation of time'. The ~6 ms burst duration is not visible in the results and stays a commonly cited figure. Note: an erratum exists (Nature, nature01221), and a full citation should mention it.

claims.claim: Serial block-face EM of zebra finch HVC shows HVC(RA) axons target almost only inhibitory interneurons close to the soma. claims.source_authors: Kornfeld J et al., Long MA, Denk W (author list from memory)

notes: live audit: The full author list, which round 1 recalled from memory, is confirmed by the search result. The results say directly that axons close to the soma target almost only inhibitory interneurons, and that far from the soma they target mostly excitatory neurons, about half of them other HVC(RA) cells. The 'synaptic-chain-like' reading is the authors' interpretation.

claims.claim: In the field cricket Gryllus bimaculatus (female phonotaxis system), selectivity for the species-specific pulse period comes from a brain network of five identified neurons and six synaptic connections. A delay line is combined with a coincidence detector.
claims.source_title: An auditory feature detection circuit for sound pattern recognition
claims.source_authors: Schöneich S, Kostarakos K, Hedwig B
claims.corrected_citation: Schöneich S, Kostarakos K, Hedwig B. An auditory feature detection circuit for sound pattern recognition. Science Advances 1(8):e1500325 (2015).
notes: live audit: Schöneich, Kostarakos and Hedwig, Sci Adv 2015 (published 11 Sept 2015) confirmed. The results state that five neurons in the female brain form a feature detector for pulse pattern, using a coincidence detector with an intrinsically delayed response (a delay line). The 'six synaptic connections' figure is stated in the companion Clemens et al. 2021 eLife abstract ('five neurons and six synaptic connections... delay line with a coincidence detector').

claims.claim: A computational model of the cricket delay-line/coincidence network, fit to recordings, reproduces neuronal and behavioral tuning in G. bimaculatus. With parameter changes alone it produces every known cricket recognition phenotype for pulse duration and pause.
claims.species: Gryllus bimaculatus (model generalized across cricket species)

notes: live audit: Clemens, Schöneich, Kostarakos, Hennig and Hedwig, eLife 10:e61475 (2021) confirmed. The results state that the model built from G. bimaculatus recordings reproduces neuronal and behavioral tuning, and that 'different song preferences, as found across cricket species, can be obtained for different parameter settings within the same circuit'. The claim's wording 'every known cricket recognition phenotype for pulse duration and pause' is stronger than the visible text. Safer wording is 'the diversity of pulse duration/pause preference types known across crickets'.

claims.claim: In the Drosophila melanogaster brain, calcium imaging of many newly characterized auditory cell types (reported as more than 20; count not confirmed) shows a continuum of preferences between pulse and sine song. Connectome reconstruction shows these neurons are highly interconnected in a network without hierarchical structure (imaging plus connectome-wiring). The contrast with the cricket's compact feed-forward detector is an interpretive comparison, not a result of this paper.
claims.source_title: Neural network organization for courtship-song feature detection in Drosophila
claims.source_authors: Baker CA, Clemens J, et al., Murthy M
claims.corrected_citation: Baker CA, McKellar C, Pang R, Nern A, Dorkenwald S, Pacheco DA, et al., Murthy M. Neural network organization for courtship-song feature detection in Drosophila. Current Biology 32(15):3317-3333.e7 (2022).

Using FlyWire, they mapped all synaptic connections among these types and assigned excitatory or inhibitory sign to most synapses. The neurons show a continuum of song-mode preferences and form a highly interconnected, non-hierarchical network. Suggested wording: '24 newly identified cell types'.

claims.claim: Wireless electrophysiology from pairs of Egyptian fruit bats showed neural activity correlated between the two brains (frontal cortex) on timescales from seconds to hours. The correlation was strongest in high-frequency LFP (>30 Hz), tracked how much the bats interacted, and rose before interactions began.
neurons: frontal cortex LFP and single units

claims.corrected_citation: Zhang W, Yartsev MM. Correlated neural activity across the brains of socially interacting bats. Cell 178(2):413-428.e22 (2019).

The correlation was most prominent in high-frequency LFP (>30 Hz), followed by local spiking. It depended on a shared social environment, covaried with the amount of social interaction, and rose before interactions began. One nuance not covered by the claim: the correlation depended on the bats sharing a social environment.

claims.claim: In groups of Egyptian fruit bats, single frontal-cortex neurons tell apart the vocalizations of specific individuals, and their activity is restructured across social contexts. Inter-brain correlation is absent during trained vocalizations.

The specific results (single neurons telling apart individual callers, restructuring across contexts, inter-brain correlation absent during trained/task-induced vocalizations) are not in the result text. They fit my recall that inter-brain correlation patterns were specific to spontaneous interactions.

claims.claim: In an observer Egyptian fruit bat, a subpopulation of dorsal CA1 hippocampal neurons encodes the position of a demonstrator bat in allocentric coordinates (social place cells). About half of them also encode the observer's own position.

claims.source_authors: Omer DB, Maimon SR, Las L, Ulanovsky N

The results say directly that in an observational-learning task a subpopulation of the observer's dorsal-CA1 neurons encoded the demonstrator's position in allocentric coordinates, and that about half also encoded the observer's own position.

claims.claim: Two-photon calcium imaging in the inferior colliculus of awake big brown bats (Eptesicus fuscus) found individual neurons selective for social calls or for navigation (echolocation) calls, allowing robust population decoding of call category. An extra finding: responses switched sharply at the category boundary when calls were morphed.

claims.claim: In the bat Carollia perspicillata, auditory-cortex neurons show spike patterns that distinguish upcoming echolocation calls from communication calls several hundred ms before vocal onset. The same activity reflects the number of syllables in a communication sequence.

claims.claim: In captive marmosets, phee calls in natural pair exchanges carried acoustic features that predicted which individual was addressed, which the authors interpret as vocal labels. In playback via a computerized system, marmosets responded more consistently to calls directed at them. Family members used similar labels and shared acoustic features, suggesting learning. This is a single-lab result; the 'name' interpretation is debated and awaits replication.

The results state directly that the study analyzed phee-call dialogues using machine learning and real-time playback, that marmosets respond more consistently to calls directed at them, and that family members use similar labels. Two items in Learning & Behavior (2025), the authors' 'A response to Jaakkola (2025)' (PubMed 40866605), show a published critique and reply, which supports the claim's 'debated' caveat. 385(6712):996-1003 was not visible in the results.

claims.claim: In marmosets, theta-band power rises in both frontal and auditory cortex shortly before a call starts. Increased directed signaling from frontal to auditory cortex predicts suppression of auditory cortex and the acoustic properties of the call that follows.
claims.source_title: Frontal-auditory cortical interactions and sensory prediction during vocal production in marmoset monkeys
claims.source_authors: (author list not verified in search results)

They also state that frontal-to-auditory directed signaling increases, and that this predicts auditory-cortex suppression and the acoustics of the following call. The paper also reports bidirectional interactions under altered feedback that predict compensation. The author names were not visible in the results, so fill them in from the PubMed record.

claims.claim: In freely moving marmosets in natural conversational exchanges, model-based (GLM) analysis of frontal-cortex neurons found activity related to hearing calls, producing calls in different social contexts, and behavioral state. The functional clusters did not align with prefrontal versus premotor subfields, suggesting a distributed organization.
claims.source_title: Representing the dynamics of natural marmoset vocal behaviors in frontal cortex
claims.source_authors: (Miller lab; author list not verified)
claims.corrected_citation: [Authors to verify; Miller CT lab]. Representing the dynamics of natural marmoset vocal behaviors in frontal cortex. Neuron (2024). PubMed 39317185.
notes: live audit: The source exists: Neuron, November 2024 (PubMed 39317185; bioRxiv 2024.03.17.585423). The results describe the main result as follows. A GLM analysis of neurons across marmoset frontal cortex during natural conversational exchanges found neurons tied to hearing and producing calls in different social contexts, plus state-related activity. The resulting functional clusters did not map onto prefrontal versus premotor subfields, which points to a distributed organization. The claim's key assertion that frontal activity 'decreases during call production' was not visible, and it leaves out this main finding. Authors were not visible; Li J, Aoi MC, Miller CT remains unconfirmed.

claims.claim: Male C. elegans are attracted to hermaphrodite ascaroside cues such as ascr#8 within a preferred concentration range, via the male-specific CEM neurons. Individual CEMs in the same worm give dissimilar, even opposite-sign calcium responses, and this diversity shapes the sex-specific preference. The exact hermaphrodite response and how complete the loss is after CEM removal should be checked in the full text.
claims.source_title: Contrasting responses within a single neuron class enable sex-specific attraction in Caenorhabditis elegans
claims.source_authors: Narayan A et al., Sternberg PW (author list from memory)
claims.corrected_citation: Narayan A, Venkatachalam V, Durak O, Reilly DK, Bose N, Schroeder FC, Samuel ADT, Srinivasan J, Sternberg PW. Contrasting responses within a single neuron class enable sex-specific attraction in Caenorhabditis elegans. PNAS 113(10):E1392-E1401 (2016).
notes: live audit: Narayan et al. (Sternberg senior author), PNAS 2016 confirmed. The results state that male concentration preferences for hermaphrodite ascarosides come from the collective dynamics of the male-specific CEM class, and that CEM responses within one worm are dissimilar and can be excitatory or inhibitory. They also say CEM responses are enhanced without synaptic transmission. Worms with only one intact CEM are still attracted but without preference across all concentrations. This settles the claim's open caveat: removing CEMs down to one abolishes the concentration preference, not the attraction itself, and synaptic modulation is needed for the preference. The hermaphrodite comparison was not visible in the results.

claims.claim: NeuroPAL is a multicolor transgene that gives every C. elegans hermaphrodite neuron a stereotyped color code, so whole-brain calcium imaging can be matched to neuron identity (Yemini et al., Cell 2021). The statements that at least six labs have published NeuroPAL whole-brain datasets, and that a 2025 GCaMP+NeuroPAL strain (KDK94) improved stimulus responses, come from separate later studies that must be cited on their own.
neurons: all 302 hermaphrodite neurons (e.g., AWC-OFF in 2025 study)

claims.source_authors: Yemini E et al., Hobert O

It reports that existing GCaMP+NeuroPAL strains had suboptimal responses and that KDK94 improved behavioral and neural responses to 2-nonanone and electric stimuli. The 'at least six labs' statement was not directly verified. A likely source is Sprague et al. 2025, 'Unifying community whole-brain imaging datasets enables robust neuron identification...' (PubMed 39826553), which needs checking.

claims.claim: In the honeybee primary auditory center, identified interneurons (DL-Int-1, DL-Int-2 and bilateral DL-dSEG-LP) respond with distinct spiking patterns to waggle-dance-like vibration pulses applied to the antenna, forming at least two parallel pathways. Johnston's organ is tuned to about 250–300 Hz, the main frequency of dance vibrations.

The results confirm the topic: waggle-phase vibration pulses are detected by Johnston's organ, and inhibitory connections take part in encoding pulse-train duration. The specific interneuron names (DL-Int-1, DL-Int-2, DL-dSEG-LP) and the 250-300 Hz tuning are not visible in the result text.

claims.claim: By tracking cuttlefish chromatophores at high resolution, the authors inferred the activity of chromatophore motor neurons from how chromatophores co-fluctuate, and from that the structure of higher control levels. The result is a statistical hierarchy of motor control and low-dimensional skin-pattern dynamics.
claims.source_title: Elucidating the control and development of skin patterning in cuttlefish
claims.source_authors: Reiter S, Hülsdunk P, Woo T, ..., Kaschube M, Laurent G
claims.corrected_citation: Reiter S, Hülsdunk P, Woo T, Lauterbach MA, Eberle JS, Akay LA, Longo A, Meier-Credo J, Kretschmer F, Langer JD, Kaschube M, Laurent G. Elucidating the control and development of skin patterning in cuttlefish. Nature 562:361-366 (2018).

The results say directly that chromatophore expansion was used as a proxy for motor neuron activity and that motor neuron activity was inferred from chromatophore co-fluctuations. claims.claim: In developing zebrafish, brain-wide activity mapping plus two-photon imaging found 21 activity hotspots and biological-motion-tuned neurons in a socially activated dorsal thalamic nucleus. These neurons encode the local acceleration of fish-like dot motion and ignore global or continuous motion. EM shows they receive tectal input and project to hypothalamic social areas. Ablating the tectum or dorsal thalamus impairs social attraction but not repulsion.
claims.source_title: Visual recognition of social signals by a tectothalamic neural circuit

notes: live audit: Kappel et al., Nature 608:146-152 (4 Aug 2022) confirmed. The result shows the PDF header '146 | Nature | Vol 608'. The results state these points directly: unbiased activity mapping plus volumetric two-photon imaging found 21 hotspots and clustered biological-motion-tuned neurons in a socially activated dorsal thalamic nucleus, and these neurons encode local acceleration of fish-like motion and ignore global or continuous motion. The EM connectivity (tectal input, projections to hypothalamic social areas) and the ablation results are not visible in the result text. The phrase 'but not repulsion' in particular was not checked and should be confirmed in the full text or dropped.

claims.claim: A June 2025 bioRxiv preprint (Fish-X) reports a synapse-level EM reconstruction of the retina, brain and anterior spinal cord of a 6 dpf larval zebrafish (>176,000 cells, >25 million synapses). APEX2 labeling marks noradrenergic, dopaminergic, serotonergic, hypocretinergic and glycinergic neurons, and glutamatergic and GABAergic identities are inferred from morphology. It builds on earlier whole-brain ssEM (Hildebrand et al. 2017) and partial synapse-level reconstructions.
neurons: noradrenergic, dopaminergic, serotonergic, hypocretinergic, glycinergic neurons

notes: live audit: The bioRxiv preprint 2025.06.12.659365 exists (v1 title 'Multiplexed Neuromodulatory-Type-Annotated EM-Reconstruction of Larval Zebrafish'; v2 and v3 add 'whole-brain'). The results describe the dataset, 'Fish-X', as a synapse-level reconstruction spanning retina, brain and anterior spinal cord of a 6 dpf larva, with more than 176,000 cells and 25 million synapses. The results also show the earlier datasets were partial: Hildebrand 2017 whole-brain ssEM (Nature) and Svara 2022 synapse-level partial reconstruction (Nature Methods). Authors were not visible.

claims.claim: The MICrONS consortium co-registered calcium imaging of about 75,000 neurons in mouse primary and higher visual cortex with an EM reconstruction of the same ~1 mm³ volume, containing more than 200,000 cells and about 0.5 billion synapses. These were co-registered with an EM reconstruction of more than 200,000 cells and 0.5 billion synapses. The paper is Nature 640:435-447, published 9 Apr 2025.

claims.claim: The H01 dataset reconstructs about 1 mm³ of human temporal cortex taken during epilepsy surgery. It contains about 57,000 cells, about 150 million synapses and about 230 mm of blood vessels, totals 1.4 petabytes, and was imaged at about 4×4×33 nm. They also state that glia outnumber neurons 2:1 (oligodendrocytes are the most common cell), that deep-layer excitatory neurons can be classified by dendritic orientation, and that there are rare strong inputs of up to 50 synapses. claims.claim: NIH's BRAIN CONNECTS program, launched in 2023 (about $150M, 11 projects over 5 years), includes an Allen Institute-led project. The '10x MICrONS' figure is the claim-writer's own arithmetic.

claims.claim: In Xenopus laevis, calls come from a sexually differentiated hindbrain vocal central pattern generator. It includes the premotor nucleus DTAM (dorsal tegmental area of the medulla) and the laryngeal motor nucleus n.IX-X, which is generally regarded as homologous to the mammalian nucleus ambiguus. Sex-typical fictive vocalizations can be evoked in the isolated brain by applying serotonin or by electrically stimulating a premotor nucleus.
neurons: DTAM (pretrigeminal nucleus of dorsal tegmental area of medulla)

notes: live audit: Source, authors (Rhodes HJ, Yu HJ, Yamaguchi A; the round-1 list was from memory) and venue are confirmed, J Neurosci 27(6):1485-97 (7 Feb 2007). The finding about serotonin or premotor stimulation in the in vitro brain is confirmed. Correction: in the Xenopus literature the laryngeal motor nucleus is called n.IX-X, not 'vocal motor nucleus (VMN)', which is fish (midshipman) terminology. Related results show the vocal nuclei are n.IX-X, the raphe and DTAM. The details that DTAM lesions abolish calling and that 5-HT2C receptors are involved come from later Yamaguchi-lab J Neurophysiol papers (2009-2010), not the 2007 study.

claims.claim: Whole-brain activity mapping (TRAP2 genetic tagging plus c-Fos) in adult male mice during courtship USVs across two sessions found consistent, robust activation in the caudal periaqueductal gray. Activity in the rostral caudoputamen correlated with how many USVs were produced.

notes: live audit: Confirmed as Luo S-X, Chen S-Y, Kuo H-Y, Liu F-C, eNeuro 13(5), ENEURO.0400-25.2026 (published 6 May 2026; PubMed 42091246). The results state directly that TRAP2 tagging was combined with c-Fos across two courtship sessions in 25 brain regions, and that caudal PAG was robustly activated. The results also mention corticostriatal engagement and enrichment of activated cells in MOR1-positive striosomes. The specific finding that rostral caudoputamen activity correlates with USV count was not visible.

claims.claim: Forebrain-to-midbrain (to PAG) pathways in mice include some that promote and others that suppress vocalization. From memory: preoptic-area inhibitory neurons promote USVs by disinhibiting PAG-USV neurons, while amygdala-derived projections suppress them.

notes: live audit: The author list, recalled from memory in round 1, is confirmed along with venue and year. The results confirm that activity-dependent tracing found inputs to PAG-USV neurons, that optogenetics showed two inputs with opposite effects on male courtship USVs, and that slice electrophysiology worked out the circuit logic. The specific assignment (preoptic-area GABAergic inputs promote USVs by disinhibition, amygdala inputs suppress) is not in the visible text. It matches my recall of the paper, where the suppressing input comes from the central-medial boundary zone of the amygdala, so the amygdala side could be named more precisely. Confidence can move from LOW to MED.

new_leads_unverified.claim: A 2025 arXiv preprint presents a generative spoken-language model of marmoset vocalizations (GmSLM). Details were not checked beyond the title.

new_leads_unverified.claim: A 2025 Science paper reports hippocampal coding of individual identity, sex, hierarchy and affiliation in a social group of wild-caught fruit bats. It extends social-place-cell work (T08-14) to naturalistic group social cognition.
new_leads_unverified.source_title: Hippocampal coding of identity, sex, hierarchy, and affiliation in a social group of wild fruit bats
new_leads_unverified.authors: Ulanovsky lab (full author list not verified in this search)

new_leads_unverified.claim: A 2026 Nature Neuroscience paper on cortical regulation of collective social dynamics during environmental challenge came up in a search on bat group vocal communication. Its species and authors were not verified; it may be a follow-up from the Yartsev lab.

new_leads_unverified.claim: A 2025 study pooled whole-brain NeuroPAL imaging datasets from multiple labs to improve neuron identification and to analyze what determines neuron position in C. elegans. It is the likely source for the 'multiple labs published NeuroPAL datasets' statement in T08-21.
new_leads_unverified.source_title: Unifying community whole-brain imaging datasets enables robust neuron identification and reveals determinants of neuron position in C. elegans
new_leads_unverified.why_it_matters: T08-21 needs its own citation for the 'at least six labs' statement, and this paper is the probable source.

The MIT licence, Brian 2 use, install time, several-GB output size and the 10.17617/3.CZODIW archive DOI were not visible in the results.

claims.claim: A leaky integrate-and-fire model of the whole FlyWire brain predicted the neurons involved in taste-to-feeding (sugar/water) and mechanosensory grooming pathways. It covers feeding (gustatory) and grooming (mechanosensory) circuits and generates experimentally testable hypotheses. The paper's scope as described does not include courtship. The specific optogenetic and imaging validation subset was not detailed in the results.

claims.claim: Pan-neuronal calcium imaging in head-fixed flies found that responses to auditory stimuli, including courtship-song components, are diverse and widespread across the central brain in both sexes, not confined to the canonical AMMC/wedge auditory pathway.
